characters.signature_detail: The deck (blue backs, #24447A), the cigarette, the lighter. When he takes the cigarette down and drops it before the standoff, his silhouette loses its signature, so he is visibly no longer himself, matching the script's note that he 'hasn't sounded like himself'. His jacket ends the scene over Deena's throat.
characters.colour: Card-stock #EDE6D6 card slugs with pip-ink type; card-back blue #24447A
characters.motion_trait: Showman arcs: riffles, fans and flicks with 15% overshoot on every gesture, 'a poor magician pretending to be a professional'. As fear grows the arcs shrink to a tremor. By the lighter, the only thing moving is his thumb on the wheel: a 9 Hz tremor of 1.5 px.

characters.name: Kay
characters.visual_design: Late 20s, shoulder-length straight black hair, soaked at arrival: 20-30 tiny specular dots of rain on the hair mass, which dry out over the arrivals. Rain-slate trench coat (#5D7480) shed to a deep red top. Red lipstick, red nails. Skin #E2B996.
characters.signature_detail: The lip mark on the rim of a glass still holding its first pour, and her lean in the doorframe. After she leaves for the loo she is never shown whole again: a red sleeve at the frame edge, defocused hair behind a glass, the lip mark.
characters.colour: Lipstick #E0485C
characters.motion_trait: The stillest person in the film. Unhurried 0.6 s ease-in-outs; she leans rather than stands. She is the one who closes distance (the shoulder squeeze), and the only person who ever walks through the gap.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Instrument Serif Italic, 56 px, #E0485C. She enters like condensation on glass: opacity 0 → 1 while blur goes 10 px → 0 over 14 frames, with a 20 ms per-letter stagger and a faint breath-fog patch (radial white at 6%) behind the words. Her lines are placed in the space between her and Scott, often spilling into his side: the 'almost a question' zone. Her full stops are tiny smudged lipstick dots. They exit by evaporating from the edges inward over 0.8 s. Her last line, 'Big night for you.', never evaporates. It stays on the corridor wall at 8% opacity in every later hallway shot, and is gone when the procession passes the bathroom door.

characters.name: Christof
characters.visual_design: Late 20s, solid build, auburn curly mop and a short full beard (both silhouette shapes). Bottle-green corduroy jacket (#2E4A3A) with fine vertical cord lines; ruddy cheeks (a soft red radial on the lit side). Skin #E8B9A0. A biscuit in his hand throughout the story.
characters.signature_detail: The biscuit and the bottle-green. The bottle that lands on the table without him is the same green as his jacket. In the oven reveal, the green cord lines are what we read before anything else.
characters.colour: Story amber #F4A85C (type), bottle-green #2E4A3A (costume)
characters.motion_trait: Big, warm, spring-loaded storyteller gestures: hands fly open and recoil, shoulders bounce on punchlines, he leans into other people's space. Gesture springs use stiffness 180, damping 12.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Fraunces (opsz 144, wght 800, SOFT 100, WONK 1), 70-96 px, #F4A85C. Words pop in one at a time on a damped spring: scale 0.6 → 1.12 overshoot → 1.0 over about 350 ms, each with a random ±4° tilt, and the line arcs upward like a gesture. He takes space: his lines sit high and may overlap other people's heads. Punch words ('twelve-quid', 'exposure', 'evidence') scale x1.3. Exit: words fall away under gravity (40 px drop plus fade, 40 ms stagger), the story landing. The joke that dies, 'Maybe you don't get to play.', is set to critical damping: no bounce, 58 px, it lands flat. 'And don't touch my cards.' is the last amber we see. The gasp and the crash get no type at all; amber simply never appears again.

characters.name: Marina
characters.visual_design: Late 20s, slim, sleek low chignon pinned with a pen, burgundy fine-knit turtleneck (#6B1424). Three silver rings on her right hand. Skin #A87452. Straight posture, elbows in.
characters.signature_detail: The rings, and the wine rings she wipes away. Her ringed right hand recurs: in Scott's left hand during the circle, trembling on his shoulder in the photo, and finally as a bloody palm print on the kitchen floor with three pale ring-shaped gaps across the fingers. That is how we know whose print it is.
characters.colour: Card-stock #EDE6D6 type with wine-ring #9C2A3D marks; burgundy #6B1424 costume
characters.motion_trait: Precise, right-angled economy. She squares things: rotates the coaster 3° to line up with the table edge, wipes in one straight stroke. The photo is the first time she is imprecise, her hand on Scott's shoulder trembling at 7 Hz, 1 px.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Spectral 500 (emphasis in 600 Italic), 54 px, card-stock white. A hairline baseline rule (0.75 px at 30%) draws first, in 200 ms. Then the line wipes on left to right at a constant 900 px/s with linear easing, like a pen plotter. Lines snap to the frame's thirds grid. Once a line completes, a wine ring draws around its key word in 300 ms: an imperfect 3 px circle in #9C2A3D at 75%, with one thicker 'pooled' arc (e.g. around 'live' in 'The table's going to live.'). Lines exit by wiping off left to right; the ring lingers 1 s longer. When she is afraid the baseline shakes and lines tilt 1°. 'No. I gave it to--' stops wiping mid-line and hangs there. When she vanishes, her last wine ring is left floating in the kitchen doorway with no text inside it.

characters.name: Dispatcher
characters.visual_design: Never seen. She exists only as the call strip: a bottom band 9% of frame height holding a live rolling waveform (4 s window, 2 px bars on a 4 px pitch), the call timer ('999 · 04:44') and a two-line live transcript. The phone UI is generic, modelled on no real brand.
characters.signature_detail: The call timer, the only clock in the film that never jumps. Her waveform is smooth and even where Scott's clips.
characters.colour: Screen white #E6EEF5 on umber. Her waveform is screen white at 70%; Scott's waveform segments are ember #FF5A14 at 70%, so the two voices read apart.
characters.motion_trait: Metronomic. Constant level, constant cadence: the one steady thing in the film.
characters.dialogue_treatment: DM Mono 400, 34 px, screen white at 90%, left-aligned inside the call strip. Each sentence is prefixed with its call time in IBM Plex Mono ('[04:46]'). Words appear on their syllable onsets, synced to her phone-band voice-ghost, with no motion beyond appearing; sentences scroll up like a live transcript, two lines at most. She never changes size, weight or colour, not even for 'Sir, listen to me.' That steadiness is her characterisation. Scott's address, which the script doesn't write out, appears in the transcript as redaction bars (█ ████████ ████) rather than invented words.

characters.name: The Extra / VOICE (O.S.)
characters.visual_design: No body, face, silhouette, shadow, reflection or outline, ever. It exists only as a count, as traces, and as a hand seen exactly twice (see The Extra).
characters.signature_detail: Warmth. A permanent 4% tungsten-core radial lift sits in the seat-width gap at Scott's right, so 'something warm' has been on screen all film before anyone feels it. And one clean, unburnt hand in Scott's own skin tone.
characters.colour: None of its own. Its hand is Scott's skin #D2A07F, perfectly clean. Its presence is tungsten-core #FFD9A0 at 4%. Its actions happen in void #000000 frames.
characters.motion_trait: It never moves on screen. It acts only in frames we don't get (1-3 frames of void plus a skip in the time slug). Its type is world-locked and ignores camera shake.
characters.dialogue_treatment: A perfectly familiar voice is everyone's voice. The word is drawn six times on one anchor point, once in each cast dialogue face (IBM Plex Sans, Barlow Condensed, Bodoni Moda Italic, Instrument Serif Italic, Fraunces, Spectral), each in card-stock white at 22%. The overlap reads as a dense, slightly smeared consensus of the name. It is anchored in the gap, exactly where the next person in the circle would be. It is drawn AFTER post, so it is the only dialogue with no grain, halation or shake: too clean. There is no entry or exit animation: present on frame N, gone on frame N+30. Beside it the record prints a 14 px Plex Mono tag, 'SPEAKER: UNATTRIBUTED', the only dialogue in the film the record labels, because it can't attribute it.

camera_and_editing: 24 fps, about 150 shots, cut frame-exact so counts, ticks, flashes and the odometer land on the same frame. Total runtime ≈ 13:50.

THE COUNT: a locked orthographic overhead of the dining table under the pendant cone. It returns 8 times and is the film's ruler: the camera never moves, only what's on the table changes. It needs no faces, so it is the cheapest and most reliable shot to build, and it carries much of the card drama.

THE GAP: after the second click every shot of Scott leaves a seat-width of negative space on his right. Lead room points into it, and the others' blocking respects it as if by instinct. Kay is the only person who ever walks through it.

THE COUNT-PAN: whip pans that stop on each person or pile for 6-8 frames with one tick per stop. Motion blur comes from accumulating 5 sub-frames at 20% each during the whip. Used at the seven hands, the five piles and the face count. Its last stop always over-runs onto the gap, and the tick fires on empty air.
INSERTS: hands, cards, glasses, the lock, the knobs, the lighter. ECU, hard single-source light, background blurred 8-12 px. Roughly 30% of the film's shots are hands.

FLOOR PLAN transitions: a line-art forensic plan of the ground floor (card-stock lines on umber, Plex Mono room labels) with one numbered marker per person. Used three times: after the arrivals, before the hallway procession, and after the explosion. The perspective set collapses into the plan (scaleY → 0.02 with a 12-frame crossfade) and back.

EXHIBIT FREEZE: 2-frame card-stock flash; the image becomes a halftone print at -1.2°; evidence tents drop in with a 70 ms stagger and a tick each; the label types in Plex Mono; hold 1.2-2.0 s; 6-frame dissolve back to motion. Rationed to 8 in the whole film. The 8th (the handprint) fails to complete, and after it the record stops logging.
MISSING-FRAME CUTS: wherever the extra acts, 1-3 frames of void are spliced in and the time slug skips, flagged in red.

Camera movement: locked frames or slow push-ins (0.6% scale per second) through the party. Handheld begins at the hand circle (0.4 Hz drift ±2 px plus 3 Hz jitter of 0.5 px), rises to 6 px in the kitchen, and the explosion shakes 18 px decaying over 0.6 s with a 2-frame 1.08x punch-in. The final shot is perfectly locked.

Match cuts: wine ring on the table → blood pooled under Christof → the ring-gapped handprint. Angelo's card flip → the oven door dropping. Title tally strokes → the fence slats in the yard. Kay's lip mark on the glass → the line drawing across Deena's throat.

Shallow-focus dialogue: in group scenes, background banter is rendered as out-of-focus type (6 px blur, 40% opacity) behind the foreground exchange, so the focus pull happens on the words, not only the faces.

Pacing map: cold open 0:00-0:40 (average shot length 5 s) | title/rewind to 0:50 | arrivals to 2:15 (ASL 5 s, comedy timing) | living room to 3:05 | seven hands to 4:10 (ASL 3 s) | skipped card to 4:50 | Kay leaves to 5:15 | five cards to 5:35 | later game/gasp/bottle to 6:50 | five piles to 7:10 | hand circle to 8:05 (ASL 2 s with 3-4 s holds) | photo to 8:45 | hallway/kitchen to 9:25 (one 15 s tracking shot) | oven to 9:40 | Deena to 10:15 | Marina gone to 10:55 | lighter standoff to 11:45 (ASL 4 s, held) | explosion to 12:10 (4-frame cuts) | ending call to 12:55 | ending hands to 13:40 (closing on a 12 s hold) | coda to 13:50.

Intensity curve (0-10): 3 cold open, then a reset to 1 in the arrivals rising to 2 at the second click; 4 seven hands; 5 five cards; 6 gasp/crash; 7 hand circle; 7.5 photo; 6 hallway (the held breath); 9 oven; 10 Deena; 9 Marina/handprint; 8.5 lighter (sustained, no release); 10 explosion; a controlled descent to 4 for the call; a final spike to 8 on 'Two.'
Record brackets: the corner viewfinder brackets inset from 3% in the arrivals to 7% in the kitchen, so the frame literally tightens. They vanish with every other overlay at 'Two.'
intensity_devices: The truthful tally: deaths are announced in the corner before the characters know. Every drop is dramatic irony, and viewers start watching the corner instead of the faces, which is exactly where they aren't looking when Marina goes.
The rule reversal: at 'six people apparently playing' the record AGREES with the picture (06). Agreement becomes the most frightening signal in the film.
The Gap held in every composition, so the audience stares into empty space waiting for something that never appears.
Missing-time frames: void black plus a red Δ skip. The extra's actions are felt as an edit the viewer didn't make.
Subliminal gas hiss: it enters at -54 dBFS the moment Christof leaves the table and rises 2 dB a minute, unexplained until the kitchen.
One beat too many: from the second click the diegetic party music inserts a 5/4 bar every fourth bar. The room feels wrong before anyone says so.
Souring count ticks: each tick detunes 7 cents further flat, so by the end counting itself sounds wrong.
Silence drops before shocks: 18 frames of absolute silence before the oven door; Deena's death keeps only her breath.
The fridge swell: +14 dB with all other buses ducked -18 dB at 'the refrigerator suddenly feels loud', used as a pressure pedal at the hand circle.
Exhibit freezes that FAIL: the record's tidy punctuation half-renders at the handprint and then stops entirely. The safety structure collapses just as the violence starts.

Typographic pressure: lines grow, scrims thin, lines collide and stack. Angelo's cards go from flying to dropping to face-down, Christof's spring dies, Deena's slam goes soft, and Marina's baseline shakes.
Scott's caret as a clock: it blinks at 530 ms through every silence and the edit counts it (the cold open cuts on the seventh blink).
A shrinking frame: the record brackets inset from 3% to 7%.
ASL compression from 5 s to 2 s to 4-frame blast cuts, broken by long locked holds that refuse release ('Sorry about your house.', 'nothing he can do but watch').
The rewatch hook: HEADCOUNT reads 02 in the cold open, Scott's free arm is always cropped out of frame, and the coda timer stops on the cold open's exact second.

key_sequences.treatment:
Opening: 18 frames of black and silence, then the tinnitus fades in alone. Before any image, the record arrives: the call strip rises at the bottom with the timer already running at 999 · 04:44 and the waveform live, and the dispatcher's transcript types 'Sir? Stay with me. You said there were six people.'
The house: the image fades up through heat shimmer on a locked wide of the burning house. Fire breathes through smashed windows. The upstairs curtain lifts on a noise-driven hem, then burns away through a rising noise-threshold dissolve with a 3 px ember edge.
Scott: a medium from his left. He sits on the grass in grey socks and a torn shirt, arm blistered, phone at his LEFT ear lighting his cheek cool white, the fire a back-key. His right arm runs down out of frame into dark grass, and every cold-open framing crops it (a rewatch shows why).
The exchange: 'Yeah.' types. 'How many got out?' Glass breaks inside as a sparkle burst in an upstairs window. 'I' types, then '--', and the caret blinks. Six blinks at 530 ms; on the seventh, SMASH TO BLACK.
Record: HEADCOUNT reads 02 at 30% top-right, never explained. Slug: SCOTT'S BACK YARD · 23:52:13.

On black, five tally strokes scratch in (four verticals and the diagonal gate) in a 14 px dry-edged card-stock brush, each with a count tick. A sixth stroke follows. Then a seventh tick sounds, and no stroke appears. Hard cut to ONE TOO MANY in Archivo (wdth 62 / wght 900) at 180 px, with 'FROM THE SCREENPLAY BY OSITA MILES' in Plex Mono 16 px beneath. The slug digits then spin backwards from 23:52:20 to 19:58:40 in 1.2 s over a tape-rewind whine. The call strip collapses to a flat 1 px line that stays faintly at the bottom edge for the whole party, waiting. EARLIER prints in Plex Mono.

Opening inserts: warm and funny, holds of 4-6 s. ECU: Scott's hand scoops crisps, half miss, and he puts them in the bowl anyway. A slow lateral push along SIX glasses: each gets a soft tink and a tiny Plex Mono numeral 1-6 by its rim, teaching the record's habit while nothing is wrong. HEADCOUNT 01.
Deena and Angelo: every time the front door opens, a rain-slate wedge spills across the floorboards and the rain swells. Deena walks straight in, and 'YOU MOVED THE SOFA.' slams in yellow with a leader line to the sofa. HEADCOUNT ticks to 02, then 03, as she and Angelo cross the threshold. Angelo's cigarette bit plays as a card exchange; 'It's decorative.' lands at a jaunty 10° tilt.
Kay: rain beads in her hair, a drip trail from the ice bag. 'Almost a question. Neither asks it' is a held 2.5 s two-shot with the music ducked 6 dB, and in the space between them Scott's caret blinks with no text. HEADCOUNT 04.
Christof and Marina arrive mid-argument and their type collides in the doorway: Fraunces bouncing over Spectral's precise wipes, Angelo's 'Finally!' card flicking in from off-frame. HEADCOUNT 06.
The second click: Scott shuts the door on the latch CLICK. Close on his hand leaving the latch, and a second, quieter, bone-dry CLICK. HEADCOUNT ticks to 07 with no one in frame but Scott. He checks the thumb-turn (locked) and lets go. Hold on the door for 1.5 s. No freeze, no sting: the only alarm is a number in the corner. From this cut, the party music gains its extra beat.

The slug jumps 20:02 → 20:51. Insert: wet footprints by the door catching the tungsten. Six treaded pairs, and one smooth pair with no tread that walks in and stops behind the couch; the record never flags it, it's a rewatch gift.
Christof's story fills the upper frame in bouncing amber while Deena's yellow, Kay's red and Angelo's cards cut in beneath: a typographic party.
Insert: Marina wipes a wine ring in one straight stroke; Scott's hand delivers a coaster without looking. 'The table's going to live.' gets a wine ring around 'live'.
Kay leans in the kitchen doorway, the first time we see that doorway, still warm here. 'Sit down, Scott.' / 'I'm sitting.' / 'You're standing.': he tilts down to his own legs over 6 frames and sits on the couch arm. Deena's almost-comment snaps half in and retracts.
Angelo pulls the deck, and card-back blue enters the palette.

Gathering: three conversations of chair-shuffling, choreographed overhead. Deena swaps her glass with Angelo's (two circles trading places), and Angelo does a riffle-and-fan flourish with 15% overshoot. The deal, from overhead: cards arc out and land with snaps.
Scott and Kay: cut to a tight two-shot. Their lines are small and close in the foreground while the table's banter goes out of focus behind them as bokeh type. 'What about Saturday?' Scott's caret types 'I'...
The stop: Deena's 'ANGELO.' slams across the frame. Audio cuts to room tone and the cards stop. Cut to THE COUNT overhead: seven piles, the seventh in the gap at Scott's right, just past the rim of the pendant cone.
EXHIBIT 01: flash, halftone, tents 1-7 drop onto the piles, label 'HANDS DEALT 7 · SEATED 6'. HEADCOUNT 07 brightens to 100% for the length of the freeze.
After the freeze: Angelo's cards resume. 'That's mine.' '...Also mine, I guess.' lands askew. Laughter as murmuring voice-ghosts. A count-pan crosses the piles: seven stops, seven ticks, the last holding 10 frames on the gap pile.

key_sequences.moment: The skipped card and the six hands (4:10-4:50)
key_sequences.treatment:
The re-deal: 'Deals again, slower this time.' Six cuts of exactly 18 frames each, one per card. Each is a medium on a person as a card slides in front of them, with a tick and a Plex Mono numeral 1...6. The audience counts along to the metronome. Cut seven lands on Angelo's place: bare walnut, and the tick that should come doesn't. EXHIBIT 02: 'CARDS 6 · DEALER 0'.
The six hands: 'Everybody touch the card in front of you.' THE COUNT overhead: six hands come down on six cards at once, a single 4-frame move with one synchronized thump. Five arms can be followed back to bodies. The sixth hand comes down on the card in the gap, and its arm fades into darkness at the wrist, beyond the cone. It is on screen 1.5 s while Angelo's deck hand pulls the eye; most first-time viewers will miss it.
Aftermath: 'One beat. Two.' is two ticks and nothing else. Christof's 'Maybe you don't get to play.' arrives with a dead spring; the room murmur dips 10 dB and no laugh comes.

Kay stands and steps around Scott's chair on his right, through the gap; she is the only person who ever crosses it. ECU of the squeeze: red nails pressing the oxford cloth, held 14 frames. 'Big night for you.' fogs on between them. A long lens down the corridor narrows to the cool strip of light under the bathroom door. The bathroom door CLICKS off-screen. Three seconds later, under Angelo's 'Okay. With Kay gone, five people. Yes?', HEADCOUNT drops 07 → 06 with one soft tick and nothing else happening. It is the first death in the film and only the corner of the screen knows. Her line stays on the corridor wall as an 8% afterimage.

'Five. It's five.' A blank card lands beside his. Overhead: four cards around the table, the fifth to himself. 'Perfect.' The record agrees with him and prints '5 / 5' over the table, but HEADCOUNT still reads 06. 'See?' The 'I'm delighted for you.' card lands crooked and he doesn't straighten it. A slow push-in (1.2% per second) on his face as the smile drains: his brows release over 2 s and his eye glints shrink. Cut to the fifth card, with a tick that never resolves.

The table: LATER, the slug jumping 21:02 → 21:46. The game is loud again: six piles, six people apparently playing, and HEADCOUNT reads 06. The record agrees with the picture for the first time since the second click, so one of these six is not real. 'Kay' is built never to be cleanly in view: occluded by shoulders, flared by the pendant, defocused behind a glass, a red sleeve at the frame edge.
Christof exits: a victory lap in amber ('That's not evidence.', with 'evidence' at x1.3), then he heads for the kitchen. The kitchen doorway is now black, and deep inside it the oven LED blinks 00:00 once a second.
Kay's glass: Scott taps it. ECU of the lip mark on a first pour. EXHIBIT 03.
The gasp: from off-screen, through a 'wall' low-pass, a short GASP and a METALLIC CRASH. HEADCOUNT drops 06 → 05 on the crash frame. A 3-frame shared flinch. 'Christof?' types and sits there unanswered.
The bottle: Scott steps toward the kitchen. A soft THUMP behind him, 2 void frames, the slug skips Δ+00:02. 'SCOTT, YOU'RE STANDING ON MY FOOT.' He looks down and moves; when he looks up, the bottle (bottle-green, Christof's colour) is on the table with five fresh glasses. EXHIBIT 04: tents 1-5, with HEADCOUNT 05 right above them. 'Oh. Thanks.' He overpours Deena's glass in a slow insert.
'Where's Kay?' / 'He did come back.' / 'This wine.': played as a slow circle of singles in which every eyeline avoids the dark kitchen doorway. The party playlist ran out at the crash, and nobody restarts it.

Overhead: four piles, then a fifth into the gap. Deena's hand catches Angelo's wrist (ECU, her hoops glinting at the top of frame). 'COUNT THOSE.' throws a yellow leader line that branches to all five piles. A count-pan across the faces: Scott, Deena, Marina, Angelo, four stops and four ticks. The pan keeps going to a fifth stop on the gap, and the tick fires on empty air. 'No.' His chair scrape cuts the room.

Setup: Angelo's cards now drop instead of fly. 'YOU'RE ACTUALLY SCARING ME NOW.' comes in card-stock white with no slam. Handheld begins. Overhead: four people link hands. Insert: Scott's left hand in Marina's three-ringed hand; his right in a hand at the rim of the light that reads as Angelo's.
First round: 'Just say who's on your left.' The VOICE's 'Scott.' appears as the six-face composite, dead still in the gap, tagged SPEAKER: UNATTRIBUTED; its unison sound is dry and too close. Scott doesn't react. The round runs Marina, Deena, Angelo, Scott. Each name lands in its speaker's own type at that person's position on the overhead, so the names build a ring on the table: FIVE names for four people, with two 'Scott.'s on screen at once.
Second round: 'Didn't somebody already say me?' The reverse round builds the ring the other way. After Marina's 'Scott.', a 30-frame pause, then 'Angelo.' in composite, in the gap. The fridge swells 14 dB as everything else ducks.
The glass: 'Whose hand have you got?' Tilt down: it is Angelo's hand, clearly lit, of course. But between them on a coaster sits a fifth wineglass. EXHIBIT 05. Marina lets go and every hand breaks on the same frame.

The handover: Marina's 'Somebody take a photo.' wipes on over a shaking baseline. CU: her ringed hand holds the phone out toward Scott's right, into the gap, without looking. The cut falls on the exact frame it would be taken: 1 void frame, Δ+00:01.
The extra's POV, the only one in the film: a generic camera viewfinder with grid lines, four yellow face-detection squares locking onto Scott, Deena, Angelo and Marina against the wall, and a shutter button. It drifts with a calm handheld, the steadiest hand in the room. Marina's hand trembles on Scott's shoulder. SHUTTER: 2 frames of card-stock white with a 6-frame decay. Hard cut: the phone is back in Marina's hand (Δ+00:01).
The photo: rendered in a different photographic language (frontal flash, flattened faces, hard wall shadows, crushed blacks). Angelo pinch-zooms in a Blow-Up enlargement, 1x → 6x in three clicks. The record lays a dashed measurement line from the wall to the camera, 'SUBJECT DISTANCE ≈ 2.6 m', and a floor-plan inset shows that point is behind Scott's chair, in the gap. EXHIBIT 06.
Who took it: 'Christof.' and 'Kay.' are said at once, so both words sit in the same spot and alternate every frame at 24 fps, an optical double exposure. 'No. I gave it to--' stops wiping and hangs. 'And Christof's in the kitchen.' is one small card that simply lies there.

The corridor: a floor-plan beat, with four markers moving toward the kitchen and an empty circle trailing behind Scott. Then one 15-second lateral tracking shot along the corridor on three parallax planes. The four walk out of tungsten and into cold, spaced with exactly one person-width between Scott and Marina. Kay's afterimage sits on the bathroom door. Scott's hand reaches for the handle and stops 40 px short, and the afterimage fades to nothing. 'Scott?' 'Yeah. Coming.'
The kitchen: cool under-cabinet light, the LED blinking 00:00, a cupboard open, a chair pushed out. A quiet HISS, which on a rewatch has been in the mix since Christof left. 'What's that smell?'
The stove: ECU, two of four knobs gone, broken plastic under the cabinet. EXHIBIT 07, the last freeze that completes cleanly. Scott hauls on the cooker; it shifts 4 px per pull with a low, wet, damp thud under the hiss.

Build-up: 'Scott, don't--', the yellow dashes stretching. ECU: his trembling hand on the handle. Then 18 frames of total silence, every bus muted, the hiss included.
The door: it drops, and the oven bulb clicks on, a small harsh tungsten box in a cold room. A reverse from inside the cavity, past a dark foreground shape, onto Scott's face lit amber from below.
Christof: a 14-frame POV insert. He is folded into the oven, read first through the bottle-green cord lines and a curl of auburn hair. His head is turned away against the back wall in shadow, limbs bent wrong across the rack bars, and a pool below mirrors the bulb like dark wine. No face, no wound detail: geometry and light do the work.
Scott: sound slams back (door-spring twang, hiss at full). His 'small sound' is his caret appearing and blinking once with nothing typed. His legs give way and the camera drops with him, 40% of frame height in 8 frames. The scream is not voiced: the dormant call strip at the bottom of the frame wakes for the first time since the cold open and its waveform clips solid red, under a muffled, saturated roar and a sub hit. Marina's 'Oh, God. Oh, God--' wipes on twice, overlapping itself; Angelo's 'No. No, no--' cards rain down unflipped.

The wound: Deena grabs Scott's shoulders. He turns into a clean MCU of her in cool light, hoops glinting. 'For an instant, she's fine': 20 frames of stillness. Then a 1.5 px card-stock line draws across her throat left to right in 10 frames at constant speed, the record's own annotation stroke. It turns wine-red and opens into a dark band that widens from 0 to 9 px over 6 frames. No blade, no figure; the doorway behind her is in sharp focus and empty. Her palms clamp over it (hand insert, fingers splayed) and her eyes lock on Angelo.
The jerk: her afro puff deforms upward as if gripped from above, a localized pinch pulled up 30 px in a 4-frame snap with a sub-thump and an air whoosh, and her head is jerked upright as she tries to fall.
Angelo: 'Dee?' He catches her with a 6-frame skid as he slips. 'Hey. Hey, look at me. Look at me.' falls as face-down cards that flip. Her breath is a wet flutter slowing from 11 to 7 to 3 Hz, then gone.
The drops: at that silence HEADCOUNT drops 05 → 04, her hoops stop catching light, and her mustard drains to ash over 2 s. A beat later, while everyone (audience included) watches Angelo hold her, HEADCOUNT drops again, 04 → 03, with nothing on screen to explain it.

The knife: Scott grabs it (ECU, the blade catching LED blue). 'Where is it?' types, deletes, retypes. 'I didn't see anybody.' / 'I know.'
The doorway: 'Marina? Marina, get away from the door.' Reverse shot: the doorway is empty, and Marina's last wine ring hangs in the air where her line would be, with no text inside. Scott won't turn his back on Angelo, so a two-shot holds standoff geometry with the gap open between them.
The handprint: ECU of the floor beside Deena, a palm print pressed in blood with three pale ring-shaped gaps across the fingers. EXHIBIT 08 fails: the halftone renders across only half the frame and the tent lands crooked, 'PALM PRINT · RIGHT · NO SOURCE'. There are no exhibits after this; the record can't keep up.
Angelo: 'I was holding her.' and 'I was right there.' land face-down and are slow to flip. 'When you counted us. You kept saying five.' He lays Deena down and covers her throat with his navy jacket: card-back blue over her.

The cigarette: the hiss is now a dense stereo band, and the score is only the hiss. Angelo takes the cigarette from behind his ear (ECU on the white stick) and his silhouette loses its signature. He drops it: it rolls a little and stops in blood.
The lighter: cheap chrome reflecting LED blue and the rain-slate glass of the back door. A two-shot on the kitchen's long axis: Scott framed by the back door (the cool exit), Angelo by the cooker, Deena on the floor between them. From 'Back door's there.' on, every card lands with no spin.
No more cards: 'Scott. Please.' is the first line with no card at all, small upright Bodoni cut on in card-stock white. 'I don't want you here when I do it.' ECU: thumb on the wheel, the 9 Hz tremor. 'Sorry about your house.' holds 2.4 s on a locked medium.
The strike: a flint rasp, a 3-frame white-gold pinpoint and six deterministic sparks, and it fails to catch. 12 frames of silence. 'Scott runs.' is a hard cut.

Outside: Scott bursts out of the door, a motion smear over 3 frames, nearly falls, and pulls the door shut by the handle. Through its glass, Angelo's silhouette stands in the cold kitchen. From inside comes the tiny dry SCRAPE, mixed impossibly close, as if in our own ear.
The blast: 3 frames of oven-LED blue as the ignition front expands from Angelo's hand and fills the windows; 2 frames of card-stock white with a ±6 px RGB split; then ember. The windows burst outward (about 120 closed-form glass shards with speculars), the camera punches 1.08x and shakes 18 px, and Scott is thrown down the steps in four 4-frame cuts. HEADCOUNT drops 03 → 02 on the white frame. The sound collapses into concussion (master low-pass at 380 Hz plus tinnitus), the exact sound of the cold open.
After: his shirt catches; he rolls, the flame shape shrinking with each turn, and crawls to the fence, whose slats echo the title's tally strokes, five and a gap. A second blast throws up a rising shower of sparks. Then a 6-second locked wide, 'nothing he can do but watch': Scott small at the fence, the gap at his right.

Dialling: LATER, slug 23:47. Red and blue strobes slide through the fence slats as faint moving bars across the grass. On a generic dial pad his thumb misses twice ('9 9 8', delete; '9 6', delete), each digit with its true DTMF tone. Then 9 9 9 and the UK ringback cadence.
The call: on connect, the strip that has lain flat since the title wakes to full width at 999 · 00:00 and becomes the dominant graphic. The dispatcher's DM Mono transcript runs; Scott's address shows as redaction bars. 'Five. I had five over.'
The names: 'He tries to count.' The five names (DEENA, CHRISTOF, ANGELO, KAY, MARINA), each in its owner's dialogue face and colour, form a slow ring around his head like the hand circle, each paired with a Plex Mono number 1-5. The numbers won't stay still: they slide around the ring, two of them read 3, a 6 rolls in with no name, digits odometer between values. The ring collapses into 'I don't know. I don't know where-- I don't know.', typed, deleted and retyped. 'Sir, listen to me. You're outside. You're safe for now.' sits perfectly steady in the strip.

The hand: 'How many people made it out?' Scott wipes his face, smearing soot. 'Me.' types slowly and cleanly, and is not deleted. 2.5 s of only fire crackle. Insert: his right hand on the grass, sooty and blistered, firelit. From his right, the gap side, a hand closes around it. It is Scott's own skin tone, warm, and perfectly CLEAN after a house fire, with no soot and no burn, its wrist dissolving into dark grass at the edge of the firelight. It is the same hand as the sixth hand on the sixth card. His fingers close back (0.5 s ease) as the score's only major chord blooms: 'Relief, so sudden it hurts.'
'Two.': typed at 140 ms per character; the caret stops and vanishes. HEADCOUNT 02. For the first and only time, Scott's number and the record's number match, and the odometer, which has carried an invisible ±0.3 px jitter since the second click, goes perfectly still. Then every record element (slug, brackets, HEADCOUNT, call strip) fades out over 2 s.
Final image: 'He lowers the phone a little.' A wide: Scott alone on the grass, right arm reaching low into shadow, no second figure. Back to the insert: two hands held, firelight on both, strobe red and blue alternating across them, the colours of the deck. The house burns and the two hands do not separate. A 12-second hold, then a 3 s fade to black.
Optional coda, for the author's approval: on black, only the call timer returns, small, bottom-left, ticking 04:38 … 04:44, and stops. That is the exact second the cold open began, so the opening happened after 'Two.', and the free hand we never saw then was already being held. THE END in Plex Mono.

sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Buses: room, fx, voice-ghosts, music, record ticks, tinnitus. All feed a DynamicsCompressor (threshold -18 dB, ratio 3, attack 10 ms, release 250 ms), then a 'concussion' BiquadFilter low-pass (normally 20 kHz, automated in the yard), then the destination. Every noise source is an AudioBuffer filled from a seeded PRNG. Each scene renders in its own OfflineAudioContext at 48 kHz from the shot table's cue list; scenes are concatenated with 50 ms equal-power crossfades and muxed with the frames. Preview uses the same graph builder in a realtime AudioContext, started at the scrub offset.

Two sine OscillatorNodes at 4186 Hz and 4210 Hz (24 Hz beating), gain 0.04, 1.5 s linear fade-in. Simultaneously automate the concussion low-pass to 380 Hz (Q 0.7) so the world sounds underwater. After the blast, recover it to 6 kHz over 6 s; hearing never fully returns in the yard.
Sines at 50 Hz (gain 0.012), 100 Hz (0.008) and 150 Hz (0.004), plus brown noise (integrated white: b = (b + 0.02*w)/1.02, scaled x3.5) through a 200 Hz low-pass at -42 dB.

White noise through a 1.2 kHz high-pass and a low-pass that sits at 1.5 kHz while the door is shut (muffled). When the door opens, ramp the low-pass to 7 kHz and the gain +12 dB over 150 ms; reverse when it shuts. Droplets: seeded impulses at about 30/s, each a 2 ms noise burst through a 4 kHz band-pass, random pan.

Two bell strikes 0.6 s apart: E5 (659.25 Hz) then C5 (523.25 Hz). Each strike sums sines at ratios [1, 2, 2.76, 5.40, 8.93] with amplitudes [1, .5, .35, .2, .1] and exponential decays of [1.6, .9, .6, .3, .2] s. Played through the room ConvolverNode (IR = stereo noise x exp decay 0.6 s).

sound_design.cue: Latch click and the second click
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: A 1-sample impulse into two parallel paths: band-pass 2400 Hz Q 6, and band-pass 420 Hz Q 4 with a 50 ms decay. The first click is sent to the room reverb. The second click is identical but completely DRY, 3 dB quieter and panned +0.15 toward Scott's right (the gap side): intimate and too close.

sound_design.cue: Party music with one beat too many
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: FM electric piano: sine carrier at f, sine modulator at ratio 1 through a GainNode into carrier.frequency, index 3.0 → 0.3 over 0.8 s, plus a tine modulator at ratio 14 (index 0.4 decaying in 40 ms). Chords Dm9 / G13 / Cmaj9 / A7b9 at 88 BPM. Bass: triangle wave through a 600 Hz low-pass. Kick: sine swept 110 → 45 Hz in 120 ms. Hat: 30 ms of noise high-passed at 7 kHz. The whole bus goes through a 120 Hz high-pass and 3.2 kHz low-pass (a small speaker) plus room reverb. From the second click the sequencer inserts a 5/4 bar every fourth bar. The playlist ends on the crash frame and is never restarted.

Glottal sawtooth at a per-character f0 (Scott 118, Deena 196, Angelo 98, Kay 208, Christof 124, Marina 220 Hz) with 5.5 Hz vibrato of ±3% and seeded jitter. It feeds three parallel band-pass formants (Q 8 / 10 / 12) whose F1/F2/F3 retarget per syllable with setTargetAtTime (25 ms). Vowel targets: a 800/1200/2500, e 400/2000/2600, i 270/2300/3000, o 450/800/2800, u 300/870/2250. Syllables come from vowel groups in the verbatim line, 140-180 ms each, with a 10 ms attack and exponential decay. f0 declines 15% across a statement and rises 20% on the last syllable of a question. Output goes through a 1.4 kHz low-pass at -26 dB, so it reads as speech heard through the noise of a party, under the type, and never as game beeps.

Her voice-ghost (f0 200 Hz) with a calm fixed cadence, through a 300 Hz high-pass, 3.4 kHz low-pass and a WaveShaper soft clip (tanh of 2x) for a codec edge. A pink-noise line floor at -48 dB. A 2 ms gate click at the start of each of her lines.

All six cast voice-ghost chains triggered on identical syllable timing in unison, summed. No low-pass (full band, so it is clearer than anyone in the room), no reverb send, mono centre, +3 dB over the ghosts. Everything else ducks 6 dB for its duration.

Riffle: 40 micro-snaps (3 ms noise bursts high-passed at 2.5 kHz) over 700 ms, spacing accelerating 30 → 12 ms. Deal 'thwip': 70 ms of noise through a band-pass swept 3.5 → 1.4 kHz (Q 2), 2 ms attack and 60 ms decay. Landing snap: 6 ms of noise high-passed at 2 kHz.

A 1760 Hz sine for 6 ms with exponential decay, plus a 3 ms noise burst high-passed at 3 kHz. The frequency is multiplied by 2^(-7n/1200), where n is the global tick index, so the roughly 60 ticks in the film sink about 4 semitones flat.

50 / 100 / 150 Hz sine stack, plus a 100 Hz sawtooth through a 180 Hz low-pass with 0.2 Hz amplitude modulation (the compressor motor). At 'suddenly feels loud', ramp +14 dB over 600 ms while every other bus ducks -18 dB; release over 3 s.

Gasp: noise through parallel band-passes at 900 Hz Q 3 and 1300 Hz Q 4, blended with a 260 Hz sawtooth at 15%; gain ramps 0 → 0.6 over 180 ms then cuts to zero in 2 ms. Crash: 9 sines at 210 Hz x [1, 1.59, 2.14, 2.30, 2.65, 3.16, 3.50, 3.93, 4.06] with seeded decays of 0.4-2.2 s, plus a 40 ms noise burst low-passed at 5 kHz, through a 0.9 s kitchen IR. Both go through a 'wall' low-pass at 2.5 kHz because they happen in the next room.

sound_design.cue: Phone shutter and Blow-Up zoom clicks
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Shutter: two 8 ms noise bursts 70 ms apart (1.8 kHz high-pass into a 3.2 kHz band-pass, Q 2), the second at 70% amplitude, plus a 2 ms click. Zoom steps: a 4 ms 2 kHz sine blip each.

Two decorrelated white-noise buffers hard-panned L/R, through a 2.5 kHz high-pass and a +6 dB peaking boost at 6.5 kHz (Q 1). Gain automation: -54 dBFS when Christof leaves the table, +2 dB per minute, -18 dBFS in the kitchen, -8 dBFS at the lighter. A 6 Hz sine LFO modulates gain at 4% depth for flutter. In the kitchen add a 9 kHz band-pass layer (Q 4) slightly offset so the two beat.

18 frames of all buses at zero first. Creak: a 70 Hz sawtooth with seeded frequency jitter through a 900 Hz band-pass (Q 8) for 400 ms. Spring: a 180 Hz sine with 9 Hz vibrato of ±6 Hz and a 1.5 s exponential decay. Bulb: a 2 ms impulse through a 3 kHz band-pass. Then the hiss returns at full level.

A 340 Hz sawtooth with 6 Hz vibrato (±25 Hz) and seeded jitter through /a/ formants (800 / 1200 / 2500 Hz), mixed 50/50 with noise, through a WaveShaper tanh(6x) and a 1.1 kHz low-pass (heard from inside his head), 1.4 s long. It sits under a 50 Hz sine hit (0.6 s) and stays low in the mix as texture. The visual (the call waveform clipping red) carries the scream.

sound_design.cue: Deena: breath flutter and hair jerk
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Breath: noise through a 500 Hz band-pass (Q 2), amplitude-modulated by a square LFO that ramps 11 → 7 → 3 Hz over 4 s and then stops; dry, centre, very close. Hair jerk: a 55 Hz sine for 80 ms with exponential decay, plus a noise whoosh band-pass swept 400 → 2400 Hz in 90 ms.

sound_design.cue: Lighter: flint wheel, failed spark, the scrape from inside
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Noise through a 3.8 kHz band-pass (Q 1.5), its gain multiplied by a 140 Hz sawtooth LFO (ratchet grain) under a 140 ms envelope. Spark: a 3 ms burst high-passed at 6 kHz plus six 1 ms crackles over 60 ms. The failed strike is followed by 12 frames of silence. The final scrape heard from the yard is the same patch dry, +9 dB and dead centre: physically too close.

Sub: a 72 Hz sine exponentially ramped to 22 Hz over 1.6 s, gain 1 → 0.001 over 3.5 s. Body: noise through a low-pass swept 9 kHz → 240 Hz over 2.2 s, then a WaveShaper tanh(8x). Glass: 60 short inharmonic sine pairs between 2.5 and 9 kHz with 20-200 ms decays, scattered over 0.8 s. At +150 ms the concussion low-pass drops to 380 Hz and the tinnitus rises for 5 s. Second blast: the same patch at 0.6x scale with the sub sweeping 90 → 30 Hz, then a shower of crackle.

Roar: brown noise through a 280 Hz low-pass with a 0.3 Hz LFO at ±20% gain. Crackle: seeded Poisson impulses at λ = 14/s, each a 4 ms noise burst through a 2.8 kHz band-pass (Q 1.2) with random gain 0.05-0.3 and random pan. Distant window glass: 20 inharmonic sine partials (2.5-9 kHz) with 30-400 ms decays through the room reverb.

DTMF digits are two summed sines for 120 ms: '9' = 852 + 1477 Hz, '8' = 852 + 1336 Hz, '6' = 770 + 1477 Hz. UK ringback: 400 Hz + 450 Hz summed, cadence 0.4 s on / 0.2 s off / 0.4 s on / 2.0 s off, through the phone band. Siren: one triangle oscillator alternating between about 925 Hz and 735 Hz every 0.5 s (setValueAtTime), through a 1.4 kHz low-pass at gain 0.04, with a slow ±10 cent detune drift for Doppler, panned -0.3 behind the fence.

sound_design.cue: Score: count celesta, sub-drone, the one major chord
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Count celesta: FM with a 1046.5 Hz carrier, modulator ratio 3.5, index 2 → 0 over 150 ms, 1.2 s amplitude decay, played only on count beats. Sub-drone from the hand circle onward: sines at 36.7 Hz and 73.4 Hz (D1/D2), the upper detuned +0.2 Hz for a slow beat. Relief chord (the film's only major chord): Dmaj9 (D3, F#3, A3, C#4, E4) as FM pads (ratio 2, index 0.8, 2.5 s attack) through a 2 kHz low-pass, rising +4 dB over 3 s as the hand closes. It holds unresolved under 'Two.' and fades out with the record.
A sawtooth exponentially ramped 600 → 3200 Hz over 1.2 s, plus noise chatter gated by a 30 Hz square wave, through a 4 kHz low-pass. Hard stop into the room tone of 19:58.

feasibility_and_risks:
The risks, most serious first, each with how it gets solved:

(1) FACES AND PERFORMANCE. Procedurally drawn faces fail fastest, so this direction never asks a face to act alone.
- No mouths and no lip-sync. Fincher top-light so eye sockets fall into shadow. Eyes are glints and lids; brows are two strokes.
- Performance moves into posture, breath, hands, light and the type.
- The overhead COUNT shot, which shows no faces at all, carries much of the card drama.
- Before production, render a turnaround and expression sheet for all six characters in the engine, under all three lights (tungsten, kitchen-cold, ember), and lock it. Any close-up that doesn't hold up becomes a silhouette or an eye-line ECU.

(2) HANDS are the film's real cast: six hands on six cards, the circle, the handprint, the final grip. Under-built procedural hands look like rubber gloves.
- A dedicated 15-joint stroke rig with layered shading, nails, creases and rings.
- A 12-pose library authored in a separate 'hand lab' page with onion-skinning.
- Inserts always lit hard from one side against shallow-focus backgrounds.
- Budget this as the single largest asset task.

(3) FIRE AND EXPLOSION. Code-generated fire easily looks like a screensaver.
- Keep flames mostly inside window openings and behind smoke.
- Sell fire through the light it throws on Scott, the grass and the hands, not through flame detail.
- Keep the explosion's key frames graphic (3 blue, 2 white) rather than simulated.

(4) NO REAL VOICES. 249 dialogue cues over about 13:50 risks feeling silent, or like a visual novel.
- Voice-ghost murmurs give each line rhythm, pitch and breath.
- Room tone, rain, music and walla keep the air full.
- The scream and gasp are sound design, not performance.
- The ghosts must stay buried (-26 dB, low-passed) or they become game 'beep speech'. This needs ear-testing early.

(5) OVERLAY OVERLOAD. This angle can slide into a UI demo.
- Most of the time the record is just two small elements (HEADCOUNT and the slug) at 55%.
- Exactly 8 exhibit freezes.
- The call strip owns the frame only in the cold open and the ending.
- Cinema comes first; the record interrupts only when the count breaks.

(6) OVER-EXPLAINING THE MYSTERY. The tally is never labelled beyond HEADCOUNT and never explained. The extra is never drawn. The record's one admission of ignorance (UNATTRIBUTED) keeps the horror open.

(7) READING LOAD AND PACE.
- Holds = 0.5 s + 65 ms per character, minimum 1.1 s; at most 7 words per chunk.
- Overlapping banter may blur into bokeh, but every plot-critical line gets clean solo space.
- Lock runtime with a type-only animatic before any art.

(8) DETERMINISM AND EXPORT.
- Everything is a pure function of t: seeded integer hashes, closed-form particles, hair driven by a convolution of past head acceleration instead of simulation, pre-generated grain tiles.
- Fonts are awaited with document.fonts.load before frame 0. All ten family/axis combinations were checked against fonts.googleapis.com.
- Expected per-frame cost at 1080p (quarter-res blur and halation, halftone, the fire buffer) is about 80-250 ms in Chrome. That is roughly 1-1.5 hours to export about 19,900 frames via WebCodecs or PNG → ffmpeg. Preview runs at half resolution.
- Audio renders per scene, because a single 14-minute stereo OfflineAudioContext holds about 320 MB of float buffers.

(9) INTERPRETIVE CHOICES TO CLEAR WITH THE AUTHOR. The script implies all of these but never states them, and none changes a word of dialogue:
- the cold-open timer loop placing the opening after 'Two.';
- 'Kay' at the later game being the extra (the record reads 06);
- the ring-gapped handprint as Marina's;
- the clean, Scott-toned final hand.

WHAT MAKES IT LOOK PREMIUM RATHER THAN CHEAP:
- Restraint: low-key light, so detail is only built where light lands.
- Frame-exact sync between counts, ticks and cuts.
- Real typographic craft: optical sizes, kerning, measured holds.
- One rigorous rule system the audience can learn and then be betrayed by.
- Grain and halation that make vector shapes feel photographed rather than drawn.

name: ONE ROD TOO MANY: a shadow theatre for seven
one_line_pitch: A backlit cut-paper puppet theatre in the line of Reiniger and wayang kulit, where every puppet is held up by a visible rod from the bottom of the frame. In every shot there is always one rod more than there are people, and the Extra is never drawn: it is a figure-shaped hole cut through the paper, letting through raw lamp-light that is too bright, and by the end it has burned the theatre down.
influences: Lotte Reiniger, The Adventures of Prince Achmed (1926): profile-only silhouettes with lace-cut detail, and the elastic hinge-joint acting.
Wayang kulit (Javanese shadow puppetry): buffalo-hide puppets with punched filigree, held up and moved by visible horn rods. The rods give this film its counting grammar.
Ben Hibon's 'Tale of the Three Brothers' (Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 1, 2010): multiplane silhouettes with smoky depth, and Death drawn as a spindly absence.
Michel Ocelot, Princes et Princesses and Les Contes de la nuit: black card against saturated, glowing gel backdrops, with the camera held at stage level.
Henry Selick's Coraline main titles: hands handling materials, with the craft of pins, fabric and paper shown up close.
Over the Garden Wall: an autumnal, lamp-lit storybook mood that turns dread into something folkloric.
Persepolis (Satrapi and Paronnaud): extreme violence carried by flat shape, negative space and a hard cut rather than by gore.
Saul Bass title design (Psycho, Anatomy of a Murder): type as a cut graphic object that slices and slides.
Coherence (2013) and The Others (2001): dread built from a wrong count of people in an ordinary domestic room.
rendering_technique:
Everything is drawn on one 1920x1080 Canvas 2D context by a pure function render(t). There is no requestAnimationFrame state. All randomness comes from mulberry32 seeded by hash(shotId, layerId, floor(t*12)), so every frame can be reproduced and exported (WebCodecs VideoEncoder plus mp4-muxer, or a PNG sequence fed to ffmpeg).

LAYER STACK, back to front:
(L0) THE LAMP. A radial gradient centred on a per-shot lamp position: core #FFF4E0, then LAMP_TUNGSTEN, falling off to SCRIM_UMBER at 1.4x the frame diagonal. Brightness = base * (1 - 0.06*D*flicker(t)), where D is the dread curve (0 to 1) and flicker is a sum of 3 seeded sines at 0.7, 3.1 and 11 Hz, stepped at 12 fps.
(L1) THE SCRIM. A 2048x2048 paper-fibre texture generated once, offscreen: fbm value noise (4 octaves) plus 3,000 short fibre strokes (0.5px, 6 to 30px long, alpha 0.04 to 0.1), drawn over the lamp with 'multiply' so the paper glows from behind. The Extra's holes are cut into this layer with destination-out, then redrawn as pure lamp core plus a 14px blur bloom. The scrim is ONE persistent object for the whole film, holding a growing list of hole paths (letters, figures, a hand), so damage accumulates across shots.
(L2 to L6) MULTIPLANE CUT-PAPER PLANES. Each plane has a depth z (0.25 = near to 1.0 = far). Parallax: screenPos = (worldPos - cam.xy) * (cam.f / (z - cam.z)) + centre. Each plane is a list of Path2D silhouettes filled CARD_INK. Interior cutouts use the 'evenodd' fill rule. Behind the cutouts sit coloured TISSUE GELS, filled at alpha 0.55 to 0.8 and then re-added with 'screen' at alpha 0.25 for glow, so light reads as passing through coloured paper.
Every plane gets three lighting passes: (a) RIM LIGHT: the same Path2D stroked 1.6px in the lamp colour, offset 1.2px towards the lamp and clipped to the outside of the shape. (b) CONTACT SHADOW onto the plane behind it: the shape drawn black at alpha 0.3, offset (depthGap*10px) away from the lamp, ctx.filter = 'blur(6 to 14px)'. This is cached to an offscreen bitmap per shot whenever the plane is static. (c) THIN-PAPER TRANSLUCENCY: fringe regions (hair, grass, curtains, Kay's wet hair) are filled at 0.85 alpha so the lamp bleeds through.
(L7) ATMOSPHERE. 30 to 60 dust motes drifting through the beam (positions are a closed-form function of t), a smoke wash in the kitchen and fire scenes (3 large blurred noise sprites), and in the fire scenes the embers.
(L8) THE STAGE LIP. A 70px ink-black rail across the bottom of wide shots, worn-wood texture with a 1px rim light. Every rod enters through it.
(L9) FILM FINISH. Gate weave of ±0.6px, seeded and stepped at 12 fps. Grain: a 256x256 seeded tile regenerated every 2 frames, at 'overlay' 6% rising to 16% with D. A vignette ellipse. Lamp-off blackouts for transitions.

CHARACTERS are articulated puppets: a tree of parts {pathData, pivot, parent, z, minRot, maxRot}, with 11 parts per body (head, jaw, torso, 2 upper arms, 2 forearms, 2 hands, 2 legs) plus character props. Each joint shows a brass SPLIT PIN: a 5px disc in BRASS_PIN with a 1px highlight arc at 10 o'clock and two 2px legs. Heads are STRICTLY PROFILE, as in Reiniger. There are no frontal faces, so nothing can look uncanny. The eye is an almond-shaped HOLE through the card that shows the lamp, with a 2px card 'pupil' bridge left inside it. Expression comes from the eye aperture (scaleY from 0.3 to 1.4), a separate brow sliver rotating ±12 degrees, and a hinged jaw (0 to 14 degrees, opened while that character's text is revealing). Each body has a costume filigree that identifies the character (see the characters list), generated procedurally as an evenodd hole pattern clipped to the torso.
Poses are keyed, eased (cubic in-out, with 6% overshoot on gesture ends), then QUANTISED TO 12 FPS: the puppets move on twos while the camera, lamp, fire and dust run on ones. The stutter reads as handmade stop-motion and hides plain in-betweens. Panic beats switch to ones. Every puppet has a ROD: a 2.2px CARD_INK line from a hidden grip point on the back of the torso down through the stage lip, with a 10px FERRULE band in that character's colour 40px above the lip.
Hand inserts use separate high-detail HAND RIGS (palm plus 14 finger segments, each pinned), drawn at 3x scale so close-ups hold up.

palette.role: Bare filament light. Used ONLY where the paper has been cut away: the Extra's holes, eye holes, Deena's wound, the final hand. Too bright on purpose.
The living-room lamp glowing through the scrim. The film's base warmth.
Scrim falloff at the frame edges and the paper in shadow. The darkest the 'sky' gets indoors.
Silhouette card stock, a warm brown-black (never #000). Every puppet, rod and piece of furniture.
Split-pin joints and lamp-catch highlights. The visible craft.
Red-wine tissue in glasses. Later the colour of blood, as translucent cellophane.
Kay's lip mark on the rim, card pips, the bloody handprint glow, the strobe-red family.
Exterior night and the rain in the doorway. Kay's world.
The gas pilot ring. It becomes the key light in the kitchen and turns the paper corpse-grey.
Burn fronts, flame tongues and the lighter spark.
Flame cores and the explosion whiteout.
Singed edges around every hole the Extra makes. They grow wider as the film goes on.
The phone screen, the dispatcher's text and the photo. The film's only cold white.
Emergency strobe through the fence slats.
Emergency strobe, alternating with red at 2.4 Hz.
Scott's ferrule and his type plate. The host carries the lamp's colour.
Deena's ferrule, gels and type plates. Wine-bottle green.
Angelo's colour. The card-back red.
Kay's colour. A lighter rain blue.
Christof's colour. Storyteller's plum.
Marina's colour. Her rings and coaster discs.

colour_arc.treatment: The scrim is lit from behind by FIRE, not the lamp: EMBER mottled with FLAME_HOT, flickering at 8 to 14 Hz. RAIN_SLATE night at the top edges. The phone in Scott's hand is the only PHONE_GLOW. A faint strobe of STROBE_RED and STROBE_BLUE leaks through the fence slats. Grain 12%. The palette promises the ending.

Full LAMP_TUNGSTEN warmth indoors at 100% lamp, grain 6%. Each time the front door opens, a RAIN_SLATE rectangle with diagonal rain streaks cuts into the warm room. Each guest enters with their own colour gel, so the room fills with colour one character at a time.
The richest part of the film: wine gels glowing in six glasses, the Kay lip mark in LIPSTICK, all six ferrule colours present. The lamp sits at its warmest. D = 0.05.

colour_arc.section: Seven hands to the second wrong count
colour_arc.treatment: The lamp drops 4% per count error and starts its slow flicker. The scrim falloff tightens: the vignette moves from radius 1.4 to 1.15. The first holes appear in the scrim, faint, with CHAR edges only 1px wide.
A sliver of PILOT_BLUE appears along the kitchen doorframe in every dining shot. The lamp is at 80%. Wine gels darken toward #4A0814. The VOICE letters burn in LAMP_CORE and stay as holes.
The phone screen's PHONE_GLOW becomes the key light on the four faces from below. The amber lamp drops to 65%. The scrim is visibly perforated.

The amber lamp is OFF. The kitchen is backlit only by a PILOT_BLUE ring light. Card stays CARD_INK but the rim light turns blue, and the scrim reads a grey-blue (#2C3442). Blood is WINE_GEL cellophane lit from behind, the only warm colour left.
Four single-frame cuts to LAMP_CORE white, then the blue again. Deena's wound and the handprint are the only warm-red light sources.

Near-total dark: lamp at 8%. The light comes only from the PILOT_BLUE burner and from every hole the Extra has cut through the film, glowing LAMP_CORE like a field of stars. One EMBER spark at the failed strike.
The paper BURNS THROUGH. An EMBER burn front sweeps out from the lighter, leaving CHAR edges and revealing FLAME_HOT whiteout. 12 frames of pure #FFE7A8, then exterior fire.

Fire EMBER behind the scrim, with STROBE_RED and STROBE_BLUE alternating through the fence slats at 2.4 Hz. The final hand close-up is lit warm by the hand-shaped LAMP_CORE hole. At the very end the lamp, fire and strobes fade to black, but the hand-hole stays lit for 48 frames after everything else is out.

typography.title_face: IM Fell English SC. Its old letterpress roughness matches cut paper, used for the title card ONE TOO MANY, the credit 'by Osita Miles' and the playing-card chapter cards. The title is cut out of the scrim as LAMP_CORE light, with one extra 'O' that is a hole.
typography.dialogue_faces: Scott: Archivo, a variable font with a wdth axis of 62 to 125, so his letters can physically narrow under pressure. Deena: Anton. Angelo: Alfa Slab One, on playing-card plates. Kay: Caveat. Christof: Fraunces italic, with the SOFT and WONK axes on. Marina: Bodoni Moda. Dispatcher: IBM Plex Mono. VOICE (O.S.): no face of its own. It borrows the face of the person it is imitating and is rendered as holes cut through the paper.
typography.utility_face: IBM Plex Mono at 18 to 22px for the scene slugs ('INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EARLIER', set in small caps at 30% opacity, top-left, 1.5s), timecode and editor overlays. It is also the dispatcher's face, so the cold clinical voice of the outside world is the same voice that labels the film.
typography.rationale: Every face is chosen for who the character is and for how it behaves when animated. Scott's Archivo can narrow continuously (wdth = 100 - 38*D), so his anxiety is measurable on screen. Deena's Anton is blunt and condensed: she says the fewest words and asks the sharpest questions ('Who's that for?', 'Count those.'). Angelo's wood-type slab looks like a card index, the loud, showy dealer. Kay's Caveat is the only handwriting in the film, the person Scott can't quite hold onto. Christof's wonky soft italic is a storyteller's flourish. Marina's hairline Bodoni is her precision ('It's the same light'). The Dispatcher's mono is the outside world. The VOICE never gets a face: it steals one, which is the creepiest choice, because it sounds 'perfectly familiar'. Legibility: dialogue is a minimum of 40px at 1080p, key lines 72 to 140px, and every face sits on its own contrasting plate except the VOICE, which is pure light on dark paper and is the most legible thing in any frame. Hold time = max(1.1s, 0.4s + 0.065s per character), and no more than 2 lines are on screen at once. Crosstalk is staggered 6 frames apart and stacked by speaker position.

characters.name: Scott
characters.visual_design: Lanky and slightly stooped, the tallest puppet at 0.36 of frame height in a wide. Narrow torso with an untucked shirt-tail flap on its own hinge, rolled sleeves, and a tea-towel over one shoulder in the party scenes. The profile has a soft nose and a worried brow sliver set a little too high. In the cold open and the ending: torn shirt (the silhouette edge ragged with 40 jagged vertices), sock feet, and a blistered arm marked by pinprick holes that glow EMBER.
characters.signature_detail: His costume filigree is the HOUSE: tiny four-pane window cutouts down his shirt-front placket, like a row of lit windows. In the ending those cutouts glow EMBER, as if he is carrying the burning house.
characters.colour: SCOTT_AMBER #E9A23B, the host carrying the lamp's colour.
characters.motion_trait: Hovering. He never settles: a 2px weight shift between his feet every 1.5s, and a 1-frame 'hitch' (a nervous double-take) before every reaction. Moves on twos. On 'I'm sitting' / 'You're standing' he looks down at his own legs in two hard 4-frame poses. From the kitchen onward his rod shakes ±1.5px at 9 Hz.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Archivo 500 at 44px on a torn strip of amber tissue (SCOTT_AMBER at 70% alpha, rough deckled ends), pinned at the upper-left corner by a brass pin beside his head, on the side he is facing. Words land 2 frames apart, each dropping 6px with a 3px overshoot: he hurries. The wdth axis = 100 - 38*D, so by the kitchen his letters are visibly squeezed (wdth 62). Interrupted lines ('I didn't--', 'I was going to text you about Saturday', 'Angelo--', 'You don't have to--') TEAR at the dash: the strip rips along a jagged edge, and the cut-off half falls under gravity (1800px/s², rotating 40°/s) out of frame. In the cold open 'I--' is torn after one letter. 'Where is it?' is set uppercase with the strip shaking. His final 'Me.' is 120px Archivo 300 at wdth 62, centred, with no plate (he has nothing left). 'Two.' is the same size at wdth 100 (the squeeze releases), and every letter casts TWO soft shadows, offset left and right.

characters.name: Deena
characters.visual_design: Compact and upright, with a sharp jaw, a high bun with two loose strands (separate fringe pieces that sway), hoop earrings as ring cutouts, and a short jacket with a pointed collar. Her profile has a decisive, slightly upturned nose and narrow eye holes: she sees things.
characters.signature_detail: Her costume edges are cut with PINKING SHEARS: every outer edge of her jacket and sleeves has a 4px zigzag, so she is the sharpest-edged silhouette in any group shot. Her glass gel is the same bottle green.
characters.colour: DEENA_BOTTLE #2F6E55
characters.motion_trait: Snap-to-pose. She hits each pose in 2 frames with no in-betweens and holds it. Her head tilts 8° for sarcasm. The only fluid motion she ever makes is grabbing Angelo's wrist ('Angelo. Stop.'): one 3-frame smear that cuts straight across the table.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Anton uppercase at 46px, tracking +20, on bottle-green card plates with pinking-shear zigzag edges. Entry is a 1-frame SLAP: it appears at 104% scale and settles to 100% on frame 2, with no fade. Exit: yanked straight down out of frame in 4 frames. Her accusations are scaled up to 72px with the plate thrust into frame centre: 'WHO'S THAT FOR?', 'THEN WHAT'S THAT?', 'COUNT THOSE.' One exception: 'you're actually scaring me now' is the only line she has in lowercase, at 38px, with no zigzag (a smooth-edged plate), and it fades in over 10 frames. Her softness is visible. In the kitchen, 'Scott, don't--' tears at the dash like Scott's lines do.

characters.name: Angelo
characters.visual_design: Broad shoulders in a loose jacket on a hinged lapel, a slight paunch, curly hair as an irregular scalloped fringe piece, and stubble as a line of pinprick holes along the jaw. The UNLIT CIGARETTE is a separate 2x26px card sliver pinned behind his ear that bobs on its own pivot. A deck of cards lives in his hand rig. The cheap metal lighter is a small rectangle with a hinged lid and a BRASS_PIN highlight.
characters.signature_detail: His jacket back is a CARD-BACK LATTICE: a diamond-grid filigree cut through the card, with crimson gel behind it, so from behind he looks like a playing card face down. The cigarette has a ferrule-like tiny white tip, the only white card in the film.
characters.colour: ANGELO_CRIMSON #B01E2E
characters.motion_trait: Showman. Big arcing card flourishes: the shuffle is a fan of 12 card pieces spreading 70° in a 10-frame arc. Dealing is a flick: each card travels in an 8-frame arc with an 18° spin. As the film darkens his flourishes are cut out and he moves on FOURS (he stiffens). In the standoff he is nearly static, except that his thumb trembles on the wheel at 1 frame per 2 at ±1px.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Alfa Slab One at 42px on PLAYING-CARD plates: bone #ECE6DC rounded rectangles with radius 14px, a crimson spade pip in the top-left corner index, and a 1px card-edge shadow. Each sentence is one card DEALT into frame from his hand: an 8-frame arc, 18° spin settling to a 3° rest tilt, landing in piles near his head. Multi-sentence lines become a fanned pile. Wrongness rule: whenever the count is wrong, one BLANK card lands after his line, an extra card with no text, which no one mentions. 'Hands. Give me your hands.' arrives as two cards slapped down flat. Then the break: 'Scott. Please.' has NO card. It is small Archivo 300 at 34px, LAMP_CORE at 80%, inked straight onto the dark scrim with no plate, and fades in over 14 frames. The script says it is 'the first time all night he hasn't sounded like himself', so for that line he doesn't look like himself either. 'I don't want you here when I do it.' and 'Go.' stay plate-less. 'Sorry about your house.' returns to a card, dealt FACE DOWN (crimson lattice back up), which flips over in 18 frames to show the line. It is the last card he ever deals.

characters.name: Kay
characters.visual_design: Slim, with a slight forward lean and long hair as a translucent fringe piece (alpha 0.82) beaded with rain: 12 tiny circular holes that glint LAMP_CORE and slide down. A raincoat collar turned up. The dripping ice bag is a translucent RAIN_SLATE gel bag with cube-shaped cutouts and drip droplets. Her profile has a softer brow and the largest eye hole in the cast, the most open face. After the bathroom she is NEVER shown complete: she appears only partly occluded, at the edge of frame, behind someone else's shoulder, or out of focus (blur 6px).
characters.signature_detail: Her costume filigree is RAINDROPS: teardrop cutouts falling diagonally across her coat. Her wine glass carries the LIPSTICK lip mark: a small crescent of #C8102E tissue on the rim, which stays exactly the same size all night.
characters.colour: KAY_RAIN #5B88B5
characters.motion_trait: The only puppet animated on ONES (24 fps) with soft easing. She moves the way Scott sees her, more alive than everyone else. Her shoulder-squeeze on exit is a slow 14-frame contact. After she leaves, every glimpse of 'Kay' at the table snaps on twos like the rest. Something else is wearing her timing.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Caveat 52px, written ON as handwriting: a clip mask reveals along the stroke direction at 18 characters per second, as if traced with a finger on a rain-fogged window. The text sits on a translucent vellum plate tinted KAY_RAIN at 35%, with 3 to 5 rain beads (4px circles) that slide down through the letters at 60px/s. Her lines linger 0.5s longer than anyone else's, then EVAPORATE: alpha 1 to 0 while the blur goes 0 to 5px over 20 frames. Teasing lines ('You did the face.', 'It really does.', 'Better.') get a 3° playful tilt. Her last line, 'Big night for you.', stays on screen after she walks out of frame and only evaporates on the bathroom-door CLICK. It is the last thing of hers we fully see.

characters.name: Christof
characters.visual_design: Round-shouldered and animated, with a wide gesture span: extra wrist joints and longer forearm pieces, so his storytelling arms sweep. Curly-topped head, a big expressive jaw hinge, and a BISCUIT always in one hand (a scalloped circle with docking-hole cutouts). Smart shirt with a chest-pocket flap. In the oven reveal the same puppet is folded at every split pin into an impossible flat stack.
characters.signature_detail: His filigree is SCALLOPS, like a biscuit crimp and a showman's bunting, along his shirt hem and cuffs. The biscuit is his prop the way the cards are Angelo's. After he goes to the kitchen, the biscuit stays on the table: it is the first object left behind.
characters.colour: CHRISTOF_PLUM #7E3F78
characters.motion_trait: Big readable gestures with 10% overshoot and follow-through on the wrist and biscuit (a secondary 4-frame lag). He leans back when delivering a punchline. His walk has a bounce of 3px per step.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Fraunces italic, opsz 144, SOFT 100, WONK 1, at 48px, set ALONG A CURVE: the baseline is a quadratic arc following the sweep of his gesturing arm, words appearing one at a time as the arm passes, on a plum tissue ribbon with curled ends. Punchlines hold back their final word: 'It was a twelve-quid DRINK.' The last word pops in 8 frames late (scale 0 to 1.12 to 1 over 6 frames) at 1.3x size. 'Exposure' in Angelo's line is set in Christof's Fraunces inside Angelo's card, a quoted voice. 'And don't touch my cards.' is his last line: after he exits, the ribbon stays pinned by a brass pin to his empty chair-back and does not fade for the rest of the dining scenes. It is still visible, slowly drooping, when the bottle comes back without him.

characters.name: Marina
characters.visual_design: Poised and narrow, with a sleek bob as one clean piece (no fringe), a long neck and a wrap dress with a crisp diagonal. RINGS on every finger in the hand rig: 3px ring cutouts glinting LAMP_CORE. She carries a folded-paper phone (a rectangle with a PHONE_GLOW screen gel). Her profile has the straightest nose line in the cast and precise, level eyes.
characters.signature_detail: Her filigree is CONCENTRIC WINE RINGS: overlapping circle cutouts like coaster stains across her dress. Wherever she sets a glass down, a ring of WINE_GEL is left on the table plane. After she vanishes, a single ring-shaped glint rolls in a circle on the kitchen floor and settles.
characters.colour: MARINA_PEWTER #A7A9AC
characters.motion_trait: Precise: linear motion with short exact ease-outs (cubic, 6 frames), no overshoot, and small movements. Wiping a wine ring is an exact 360° circle in 24 frames. Under fear the precision breaks: her hand on Scott's shoulder trembles at ±1px on ones (the only jitter she ever has), and her lines start to wobble.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Bodoni Moda 44px with high contrast, set AROUND A CIRCLE: each line wraps a 'coaster' disc of pewter paper (radius fitted to the line length, 120 to 220px). It enters by rotating clockwise 90° into place in 8 frames on a cubic ease-out and locks to an exact upright reading position. The text never overlaps another plate. Snaps ('No.', 'I can see that.') are short arcs. When she's frightened, 'Okay, that's enough. Somebody take a photo.' BREAKS the circle: the coaster cracks in two and the text runs straight, with tracking jitter of ±1px per letter per frame. 'No. I gave it to--' tears at the dash and the sliver of disc spins away. 'Scott?' in the hallway is set on a tiny unbroken disc, her last line, very exact and very small.

characters.name: Dispatcher
characters.visual_design: Never seen, and not a puppet. She exists only as LIGHT IN A RECTANGLE: the phone screen (a PHONE_GLOW gel, 1px rounded corners) against Scott's cheek. In medium shots her text projects as a soft cold rectangle of light on the scrim beside his head, as if the call is a window cut in the night. A slow 2s 'breathing' glow pulse marks an open line.
characters.signature_detail: The cursor. A block cursor blinks at 1.6 Hz after every one of her questions while she waits for an answer. In the final exchange it blinks 3 times after 'How many people made it out?' before Scott answers.
characters.colour: PHONE_GLOW #CFE3F2
characters.motion_trait: No motion except typing and the cursor: clinical and constant. Her lines never shake, even when everything else in the frame does.
characters.dialogue_treatment: IBM Plex Mono 400 at 40px, PHONE_GLOW on a near-black (#0B0F14) rectangle at 85% alpha with 1px scanlines at 6% opacity. TYPED character by character at 32 characters per second, left-aligned, with a block cursor. Her questions sit in a fixed position (upper third, inset 160px from the side Scott faces), so the eye always knows where the outside world speaks from. Key questions are set at 56px: 'How many got out?' (cold open) and 'How many people made it out?' (ending). The stage direction where Scott gives his address is shown as her text typing '[ADDRESS]', which Scott never completes on screen. The line simply cuts.

characters.name: The Extra / VOICE (O.S.)
characters.visual_design: NEVER DRAWN. It exists only as subtraction: a bare rod with no ferrule; a figure-shaped HOLE through the scrim showing raw LAMP_CORE; objects that move on rods with no puppet holding them; a second, wrong-direction rod (from ABOVE) in the moment it takes Deena; a handprint-shaped hole in the floor; and the final hand-shaped hole of warm light. Every hole has a CHAR singe at its edge: 1px at first, 4px in the kitchen, 8px with ember flecks at the end.
characters.signature_detail: THE SEVENTH ROD. From the very first frame of the film, the stage lip always holds one rod more than the number of puppets on stage: plain, unvarnished card-brown #3B2A20, with no ferrule colour. Nobody in the story ever looks at it.
characters.colour: No hue of its own: LAMP_CORE #FFF4E0, too much light, edged with CHAR #2A1208. It is the absence of paper.
characters.motion_trait: It NEVER moves on screen. It only moves between cuts: its rod or hole is in a different place after every cut, and if it ever must move inside a shot, it moves in a single frame. The one exception is the final hand, which closes in 6 frames on ones, the smoothest motion in the film, smoother even than Kay.
characters.dialogue_treatment: Letters PUNCHED THROUGH THE PAPER. There is no ink and no plate: the letter shapes are cut out of the scrim with destination-out and filled with LAMP_CORE plus a 12px bloom at 60% alpha, with CHAR edges 2px wide and 4 to 6 ember flecks. They appear on a SINGLE FRAME: a hard cut-in with no animation, as if they had always been there. They are positioned in the empty gap BETWEEN two characters, never near a speaker. The typeface is BORROWED from the person being imitated ('a perfectly familiar voice'). The first 'Scott.' is set in Angelo's Alfa Slab One, as if it is Angelo's own line, said before he says it. The second 'Angelo.' is in Deena's Anton, her exact earlier line. The letters STAY as permanent holes in the scrim of that room for the rest of the film, so the wall accumulates the Extra's words. In the lighter standoff they glow like stars. Size 64px, never larger: it is quiet.

the_extra:
THE RULE OF N+1. This is a puppet theatre, and every living thing on stage must be held up by a rod that comes up through the stage lip at the bottom of the frame. Wide shots are COUNTING SHOTS: the camera always frames low enough to show the lip, and the audience can always count rods. Puppets + 1 = rods, every time, starting from the first frame of the film (Scott on the grass, with two rods). The extra rod is plain card-brown with no ferrule band, while every friend's rod carries their colour, so a careful viewer can tell which one does not belong. Close-ups CROP OUT THE LIP. You cannot count in a close-up, and that is where the Extra does its work: every vanishing happens across a close-up.

HOLES, NOT SHAPES. The Extra is drawn by removing paper. It appears as (1) a figure-shaped absence in the scrim, a patch the size of a person where the paper fibre texture is missing, at first only 4% brighter than its surroundings and with no grain, so it reads as 'something is off with the light' and then, by the photo, as a person-sized window of raw lamp; (2) its words, punched through as letters; (3) the handprint; (4) the final warm hand. Because the scrim is one persistent object for the whole film, these holes ACCUMULATE: the wall gets steadily more perforated, and the theatre's own light leaks out of it. That is the visual form of the dread rising.

OBJECTS ON ORPHAN RODS. When the Extra 'does' something, the object moves on its own rod with no puppet attached: the returning wine bottle descends on a bare rod; the five fresh glasses are set down by a rod; the phone is lifted out of Marina's hand by a rod and returned. Most of the time the rod stays just out of frame, so we see only an object moving with no hand. The full orphan rod is revealed only once, in the photo.

COUNTING AS EDITING. Every spoken or implied count cuts ON THE NUMBER (one shot per count beat), each with the rod-tick sound. The CHAPTER CARDS are cut-paper playing cards of hearts whose pip count is the number of people the characters believe are present, each with one pip punched out as a glowing hole: a 6 at the arrivals, a 7 at 'seven hands', a 5 after Kay leaves, a 4 at the photo, a 2 at the end. The final card, the two of hearts, has no hole: both pips are present.

DISTINCTION FROM THE MISSING. A friend who vanishes leaves a different mark from the Extra: a SUN-FADE GHOST, a pale silhouette slightly lighter than the scrim, like the outline where a picture once hung, which fades over 4 seconds. Their rod is pulled down through the lip, one 3-frame drop with a soft wooden knock. The Extra's holes never fade.
camera_and_editing: A virtual multiplane camera with x, y, zoom and z on every shot. Moves are slow dollies at 2 to 6% of frame per second with cubic easing, run on ones (24 fps) so they glide over puppets that move on twos. That contrast is the core of the premium handmade look.

Shot grammar: WIDES are stage-level and show the stage lip and rods, so they work as counting shots. MEDIUMS crop at the waist. CLOSE-UPS are profile heads at 0.6 of frame height with the eye hole fully lit. INSERTS (hands, cards, glass rim, lighter wheel) use the 3x hand rigs with a shallow 'depth of field' (blur 4 to 10px on planes away from the focus z, done with ctx.filter and cached per shot).
Rack focus by animating per-plane blur, used on reveals: the fifth glass, the empty hallway, the handprint.
