Rising tempo by section: arrivals average 5 to 7s per shot; the party 4s; seven hands 2.5s; the hand-circle 1.5s, cutting on each name; the kitchen 0.8 to 1.2s; Deena has single-frame LAMP_CORE flash cuts. The lighter standoff then breaks the pattern with one unbroken 38-second take, a slow push from a medium two-shot to Angelo's thumb on the wheel. The stillness is unbearable after all that cutting.
Cut-on-count: every count (cards dealt, names in the circle, 'Four. There's four of us') gets one cut per number, with the rod-tick sound.

Transitions between scenes are LAMP-OFF BLACKOUTS: 4 frames of black with the filament afterglow fading (a radial gradient of LAMP_CORE at 20%, falling to 0 over the 4 frames), then the lamp clicks on to the new scene. The puppeteer is resetting the stage. There are no dissolves.
Gate weave of ±0.6px and a scale breath of 0.3%, seeded per 12 fps step, so the frame feels physically projected.
Camera shake comes only from physical events: the metallic crash (8 frames, ±6px), the explosion (30 frames, ±24px decaying exponentially), and the second explosion (smaller).
Never cross the lip: the camera never shows the puppeteers or what is below the stage. The rods come from below, and from nowhere else, except once (Deena).
intensity_devices: THE ROD COUNT: one rod too many, in every wide shot. Viewers who notice it get a dread the characters don't have, and attentive viewers start counting every wide.
THE PERFORATING WALL: the scrim accumulates the Extra's holes (VOICE letters, figure patches), so later frames literally leak more light. By the standoff the room is lit only by those holes.

THE DREAD CURVE D(t), from 0 to 1, a single number driving the lamp level (100% down to 8%), flicker amplitude, grain (6% to 16%), vignette radius (1.4 to 0.95), the CHAR width on holes (1px to 8px), the scrim's umber falloff and Scott's type width (wdth 100 to 62). D steps up at every wrong count, never smoothly, so each count error is felt as a notch.

THE FRAMERATE LEVER: normal acting is on twos. Panic beats (Scott's scream, Angelo catching Deena, Scott running) jump to ones, and dread holds freeze completely (no gate weave) for 1 to 2 seconds. The stillness reads as the world stopping.
TEMPO COMPRESSION: shot lengths shrink from about 6s to about 0.8s, then the 38s single take at the lighter.
SILENCE BEFORE THE HIT: the soundtrack ducks to the lamp hum alone for 0.5 to 0.8s before the gasp, the oven door, Deena's wound and the lighter strike.

THE HEARTBEAT BED: a synthesized heartbeat enters at the seven hands (at 58 BPM, -30 dB) and rises with D to 112 BPM in the kitchen. In the ending a SECOND heartbeat joins it, out of phase, and drifts into lockstep.
THE SHEPARD RISE: from the hallway onward an endless rising Shepard-Risset glissando hides under the gas hiss, so the tension never resolves.
TYPE UNDER PRESSURE: Scott's letters narrow, torn strips fall, Marina's circle breaks, Angelo loses his card, and the VOICE's letters never go away.
THE EXTRA BLANK CARD: every time the count is wrong, a blank card lands after Angelo's line. It is never acknowledged and gets more frequent.
LEFT-BEHIND OBJECTS: Christof's biscuit, his pinned ribbon line, Kay's lip-marked glass, Marina's ring. The frame keeps holding small things that belong to people who aren't there.

key_sequences.treatment: Start on 2s of black and tinnitus. The scrim catches light from BEHIND, from fire: EMBER mottled with FLAME_HOT. In silhouette, the house is a cut-paper facade on plane z=0.8, with flame tongues as 14 cut-paper flame pieces on their own pivots, waving on twos (rotation ±12° at 2 to 4 Hz, phase-offset), plus 200 deterministic ember particles rising on ones. The upstairs curtain is a thin translucent piece that lifts, and then the paper burns away in 10 frames (a local burn front). Scott sits on fringe-cut grass in the foreground (z=0.3), blistered arm holes glowing EMBER, phone glowing. The DISPATCHER types: 'Sir? Stay with me. You said there were six people.' Scott: 'Yeah.' (a torn amber strip, at a squeezed width). 'How many got out?' sits at 56px with the cursor blinking. Glass breaks inside: a bright tinkle, and a window piece drops off the facade. Scott: 'I--' is torn after one letter, and the remainder falls into darkness. Push in to his profile: the eye hole holds the reflection of the fire. A slow pull back reveals the stage lip with TWO rods, his amber one and a bare one beside it. HARD CUT on a lamp-click to white tungsten: the title ONE TOO MANY burns out of the scrim in IM Fell English SC, with the second O as a hole that stays lit 6 frames longer than the rest.

INSERT: the crisps bowl. A hand rig scoops crisp shapes (curled card chips), half miss, and Scott picks them up. A wide of the room at full tungsten: SIX glass shapes on the table, six chairs, and the stage lip with Scott's rod plus the bare one. The doorbell. The door is a hinged plane, and when it opens a RAIN_SLATE rectangle with diagonal rain cuts into the warm room. Each arrival enters on their own rod and adds a ferrule colour to the lip. Deena's anton slaps ('You moved the sofa.'), Angelo's cards are dealt ('It's decorative.' as the cigarette bobs back behind his ear), and Kay arrives drenched with rain beads sliding down her hair-fringe. Their almost-question is a 2-second two-shot held on a freeze-frame of their profiles with an 18px gap, with no type at all, only the room hum. Christof and Marina argue: Fraunces curves against Bodoni circles, overlapping at the screen centre like crosstalk. The door shuts. CLICK, then on the second CLICK the lip holds 6 coloured ferrules plus 1 bare rod, and the camera, for one beat, very slowly drifts down to include it. Scott checks the lock (an insert of the latch, a pinned card piece) and lets it go. Chapter card: the six of hearts, with one pip punched out as a glowing hole.

The warmest wide of the film: six puppets, six gels in glasses, Christof's biscuit arm sweeping the Fraunces ribbon. Marina's wine-ring wipe is an exact 24-frame circle, and the coaster handoff is an insert of two hand rigs. 'Sit down, Scott' / 'I'm sitting' / 'You're standing': Scott's head drops to look at his legs on the cut, then he sits on the couch arm with a 4-frame settle. Deena almost comments: her jaw hinge opens 4°, then closes. Angelo pulls the deck: a 10-frame fan flourish. In the background, the figure-shaped fibre-less patch on the scrim is visible at 4% brightness, standing between Kay and the kitchen door. Almost nobody will see it on a first watch.

Rhythm: card deal ticks at 2.4 per second, one quick cut per pile, with Scott and Kay's murmured exchange (Caveat versus torn amber) laid under the deal. 'Angelo.' (Deena) and the cards STOP: all sound drops to the lamp hum. An overhead insert, the only top-down shot so far, shows the table as a cut-paper oval with SEVEN card-backs (crimson lattice) in a ring. A hard cut on each pile, numbered by the rod-tick: 1 to 7. The 7th tick is detuned by -100 cents. Angelo's line cards then deal into frame, followed by the first BLANK card. Christof's 'Take both. You'll still lose.' gets a laugh track of synthesized murmur that cuts off a beat too early. D steps to 0.15. Chapter card: the seven of hearts.

Slow re-deal on ones (the only time Angelo moves on ones: he is concentrating). Overhead: six cards land, each on a count cut. ANGELO'S PLACE IS EMPTY: a rack focus from his hands to the bare table plane in front of him. 'Everybody touch the card in front of you.' Overhead: six hand rigs come down on six cards in a staggered 3-frame cascade; count the hands with ticks, 1 to 6. Angelo's hand is not one of them; his holds the deck. Freeze for 2 beats: no gate weave, total stillness except the lamp flicker. Christof: 'Maybe you don't get to play.' A ribbon arc, no punchline pop: the last word just lands. In the wide, rods: 6 coloured plus 1 bare.

She stands on ones, Scott's eye line follows, and her hand rig squeezes his shoulder in 14 frames: the softest contact in the film. 'Big night for you.' stays on screen as she walks into the corridor (a deep plane at z=0.9, going darker). Her KAY_RAIN rod slides out of the lip as she exits frame. The bathroom door CLICK, offscreen: her line evaporates on that click. In the lip: 5 coloured rods plus 1 bare. One beat later, the bare rod is standing where her rod was. Chapter card: the five of hearts.

'Okay. With Kay gone, five people. Yes?' Five cut-on-count deals, with the fifth to himself: perfect. 'See?' A card dealt with a flourish. Christof's 'How old are you?' pops. Then a slow 4-second push in to the fifth card while Angelo's smile drains: the jaw hinge closes over 30 frames and the eye-hole aperture narrows from 1.0 to 0.6. Behind him, out of focus, a fibre-less patch on the scrim in the shape of a seated person. No blank card this time, because the count was right. That is what's wrong.

key_sequences.moment: Christof's gasp and crash; the bottle returns
key_sequences.treatment: A later scene: noisy and chopped, Christof winning, his ribbon 'Thank you. I'll accept apologies individually.' He leaves for the kitchen, and his last line, 'And don't touch my cards.', stays pinned to the chair-back. His biscuit stays on the table. INSERT: Kay's glass with the lip mark, the wine barely touched, and Scott's fingernail tapping it (a glass ping at 1760 Hz). DUCK TO SILENCE for 0.6s. The GASP, then the METALLIC CRASH: the camera shakes and every puppet snaps up in 2 frames. Scott: 'Christof?' Nothing. Then the soft THUMP of the bottle: shown only as a medium of Scott's back with a bottle-shaped silhouette arriving on the table behind him with no arm in frame. 'Scott, you're standing on my foot.' He looks down and up: the bottle is there, and FIVE fresh glasses, set in a single frame. 'Oh. Thanks.' No one answers: the lamp hum is the only sound. Pouring: the WINE_GEL fills Deena's glass past its rim and the red spreads across the table plane. 'Where's Kay?' / 'He did come back.' / 'Yeah. This wine.' Cut on each look to the bottle in his hand. The PILOT_BLUE sliver in the kitchen doorframe appears and stays.

Angelo deals: four cuts, then a FIFTH on the fifth tick, detuned. Deena's 3-frame smear catches his wrist. 'COUNT THOSE.' at 72px. He counts: a cut per face, Scott, Deena, Marina, himself, with only four ticks. 'No.' The chair-scrape is a sharp noise sweep down. 'Is somebody messing with me?' Two cards slapped down. 'You're actually scaring me now': Deena's lowercase line, and Angelo's eye aperture softens.

The centrepiece. An OVERHEAD camera rotating slowly (3° per second) above the cut-paper table: four sleeves reach in, and the hand rigs link: Marina's warm ringed hand (pewter ring glints) on Scott's left, and 'Angelo's' on his right. 'Just say who's on your left.' Then the VOICE: on a single frame, the letters 'Scott.' in Angelo's Alfa Slab are PUNCHED THROUGH the table-paper, between two linked hands, glowing LAMP_CORE, with the wet-only reverb tone. No one reacts. The roll call cuts on each name: 'Marina.' (Scott), 'Deena.' (Marina), 'Angelo.' (Deena), 'Scott.' (Angelo, on his card), each name in its owner's style. Five names for four people. The camera stops rotating. 'Didn't somebody already say me?' 'Other way.' Second round, cut on each name. Then very softly, in Deena's Anton punched through as holes: 'Angelo.' The fridge hum swells to -12 dB. 'Scott, whose hand have you got?' INSERT: his hand IS holding Angelo's. A rack focus to the FIFTH glass between them, set on a coaster, with its own ring stain.

Marina's coaster cracks: 'Okay, that's enough. Somebody take a photo.' She holds the phone out to the side without looking. In the cut-in, her hand rig releases it and the phone rises out of frame on nothing. A wide shows the four puppets against the wall, with Marina's hand trembling on Scott's shoulder at ±1px on ones. The SHUTTER: two clicks and a 2-frame PHONE_GLOW whiteout. The phone is back in her hand. A close-up of the screen: the photo is a miniature shadow-play inside the phone rectangle, four silhouettes against a pale scrim, with the stage lip visible in it. FIVE RODS. The fifth rod rises to the top edge of the photo, to exactly where a camera would be held, and ends in nothing. Deena: 'Four. There's four of us.' Angelo's pinch-zoom is a scale animation of the phone image. 'Who took it?' 'Christof.' and 'Kay.' arrive SIMULTANEOUSLY, a Bodoni circle and an amber strip overlapping in the same frame. Both look to the empty hall: a slow pan to the corridor, where the bathroom door is a dark plane. 'And Christof's in the kitchen.' Angelo's card lands at 34px instead of 42px, because he doesn't raise his voice. Chapter card: the four of hearts.

The lamp goes OFF with an audible click and the room's colour drains. A lateral tracking shot (on ones) of four silhouettes in procession at z=0.5, past the closed bathroom door (a plane with a sliver of LAMP_CORE light under it, too bright for a bathroom). Scott's hand reaches for the handle and stops 20px short; hold for 1.5s. Marina's tiny disc: 'Scott?' 'Yeah. Coming.' The KITCHEN is lit only by the PILOT_BLUE ring of the stove, from behind the scrim: cupboard door open, a chair pushed out (a slanted plane). 'Christof?' The HISS rises. Marina's line: 'What's that smell?' Insert: the stove with TWO KNOBS MISSING (empty circular holes glowing blue) and broken plastic fragments as small card shards under the cabinet. 'Oh, shit. Gas.' Rapid cuts: 'Turn it off.' / 'The knobs are gone.' / 'So turn it off behind the stove.' / 'I'm trying.' Scott grips and pulls the stove: it budges 4px, and the deep 'damp, ugly' sound comes from inside. Angelo: 'Leave it. We'll get outside and call someone.'

Scott's hand rig on the oven handle. Deena takes one step: 'Scott, don't--' torn at the dash. SILENCE for 0.7s. The door drops on its hinge (a 6-frame swing with a heavy clunk), and inside the oven a WINE_GEL red is lit from behind. CHRISTOF is a puppet FOLDED AT EVERY SPLIT PIN: limbs stacked flat over each other at angles a body can't make, a paper doll folded into an envelope. The head piece is CRUMPLED: drawn with 9 crease lines (alternating light and dark gradients along the creases) pressed against the back wall. Blood is a pool of translucent red cellophane under the folded limbs, glowing. His scalloped hem and the BISCUIT CRIMP of his cuffs make him unmistakable. Hold 18 frames, no camera move. CUT to Scott's rod DROPPING 60px through the lip (his legs give way), then his scream played as pure sound over a close-up of his face, with the eye hole wide (aperture 1.4) and the jaw hinge at maximum. No text: the scream is too big for a plate. Then Marina's 'Oh, God. Oh, God--' (the circle tears) and Angelo's 'No. No, no--' as three cards slapped down crooked.

Deena grabs Scott's shoulders and pulls back (a 3-frame smear), and Scott turns to her: a medium two-shot. 'For an instant, she's fine': hold 12 frames, perfectly still. Then a SCORING LINE draws itself across her silhouette's neck at 1 frame per 30px, an invisible blade cutting paper (a dry paper-cut sound), and the paper PARTS: the slit opens 4px and LAMP_CORE floods through, turning WINE_GEL red as cellophane drops behind it. There is no knife and no figure. Interleaved with 4 single-frame LAMP_CORE white flash cuts (frames 3, 7, 12 and 18 of the beat). Her palm rigs clamp over the light, which leaks red between the finger segments. Her eyes fix on Angelo. Then the wrongest frame in the film: a SECOND ROD comes DOWN FROM THE TOP of the frame (bare card-brown, no ferrule) and JERKS her head piece upright on its pivot. It is visible for exactly 4 frames, then gone. Angelo moves on ONES: he slips (a 2-frame foot slide in the red) and catches her before she hits the floor plane. 'Dee?' / 'Hey. Hey, look at me. Look at me.' / 'No, no. Stay. Come on, Dee. Come on.' are cards dealt straight down in a stack, not flicked, with no flourish. Her breathing is the 'wet flutter' sound, and her finger segments relax one at a time over 2 seconds. Her bottle-green ferrule rod lowers through the lip slowly, the only slow rod-drop in the film, while Angelo holds her anyway.

Scott backs into the counter: an insert of a hand rig grabbing a kitchen knife (a long blade cut piece with a BRASS_PIN rivet), shaking at 9 Hz ±2px. 'WHERE IS IT?' is an amber strip vibrating. A whip-pan sweep of the kitchen (a motion-blurred plane slide across 5 frames). Angelo: 'I didn't see anybody.' Scott: 'I know.' At the smallest Scott text in the film, 30px.

'Marina? Marina, get away from the door.' CUT to the doorway: empty, with her SUN-FADE GHOST, a pale silhouette slightly lighter than the scrim, fading over 4 seconds. Her pewter ring falls from nowhere, hits the floor plane, rolls in a 1.5-turn circle (a wine-ring path) and settles with a metal tick. The lip: her pewter rod is gone. Count the rods: Scott (amber), Angelo (crimson), one bare, plus Deena's lowering. 'She was here. She was just here.' Angelo stares at the floor beside Deena: a rack focus to a HAND-SHAPED HOLE cut in the floor paper, red light glowing up through it, with CHAR edges 4px. 'No hand remains.' 'I was holding her.' / 'I was right there.' are cards placed, not dealt. Angelo lays his jacket (the card-back lattice piece) over her throat light, which still leaks through the lattice holes in a red diamond pattern.

The lamp is at 8%. The kitchen is lit only by the PILOT_BLUE burner and by EVERY HOLE the Extra has cut so far, glowing on the scrim: the VOICE letters 'Scott.' and 'Angelo.', the figure patches, the handprint. 'The gas. Angelo, we have to shut the gas off.' Angelo looks at the stove, then at Deena. He takes the cigarette from behind his ear (the pinned sliver comes off its pivot), stares at it, and drops it: it falls on twos and bounces once. Insert: his hand rig pulls the cheap metal LIGHTER, catching a BRASS_PIN glint. Then the 38-second slow push begins, from a two-shot to Angelo's thumb, with NO CUTS. Scott: 'No.' / Angelo: 'Back door's there.' (a card) / 'Put it down.' / 'Go, Scott.' / 'Just-- think for one second.' (torn) / 'I have.' / 'And say what?' / 'I don't know.' / 'Neither do I.' The gas hiss rises under all of it. 'You always keep the back gate unlocked?' / 'Yeah.' / 'Good. Go through it. Don't stop in the yard.' Then 'Scott. Please.' with NO CARD: thin Archivo inked onto the dark. 'I don't want you here when I do it.' The thumb trembles. 'You don't have to--' is torn. 'Go.' is plate-less. A long beat. Then he looks once more at Deena. 'Sorry about your house.' arrives FACE DOWN, and the card flips in 18 frames. The wheel strikes: an EMBER spark of 12 particles that dies. Scott runs: CUT, the first cut in 38 seconds.

EXT: Scott flies through the back door (on ones, a 6-frame smear). He grips the handle to pull it shut. From inside: the tiny dry SCRAPE (a sound with no image). Then the PAPER BURNS THROUGH. On the kitchen-window plane and then the whole frame, a burn front propagates from the window centre: a seeded fbm noise field compared against a radius that grows at 2,200px/s. Pixels inside it are cut away to FLAME_HOT whiteout, the 14px band at the threshold is an EMBER gradient, and the 6px band outside it is CHAR. It is computed at 480x270 and upscaled with smoothing plus grain. 12 frames of pure #FFE7A8, then the blast hits: Scott's puppet is thrown down the steps, with its pieces swinging at the split pins on ones (shown as a physical marionette whiplash, with springy joint rotation that damps over 0.8s). Windows burst outward as 30 cut-paper shards on ballistic arcs. His shirt-tail catches and burns: he rolls, three rolls, each rotation on twos. The second explosion sends a ring of 400 ember particles up. He crawls to the fence. Wide: the facade burns, with flame pieces on pivots. For the first time since the cold open, the lip shows TWO rods: amber and bare.

key_sequences.moment: Ending: the dispatcher and the two hands (about 1.8 minutes)
key_sequences.treatment: The burning facade is backed by EMBER, with STROBE_RED and STROBE_BLUE alternating through the 9 fence-slat gaps at 2.4 Hz. Scott's hand misses the emergency number twice: the phone rectangle flickers. The DISPATCHER types: 'Emergency services. What is your address?' (her '[ADDRESS]' text cuts off), 'Are you injured?' 'Yeah. I-- yeah.' 'Help is coming. Is anybody still inside?' A window collapses inward. 'My friends.' 'How many friends?' 'Five. I had five over.' 'And are they all still inside?' He tries to count. CUT-ON-COUNT, five cuts, each a short close-up of an object left behind: Deena's pinking-shear jacket edge, Christof's biscuit, Angelo's dropped cigarette, Kay's lip-marked glass, Marina's ring. On the fifth cut the order SHUFFLES and the five inserts repeat out of sync, the numbers refusing to stay still, with the rod-tick doubling. 'I don't know. I don't know where-- I don't know.' 'Sir, listen to me. You're outside. You're safe for now.' 'How many people made it out?' (56px, with the cursor blinking 3 times). He wipes his face on his sleeve. 'Me.' at 120px with a squeezed width. Then a close-up insert at grass level: Scott's free hand lies open in the fringe-cut grass. SOMETHING CLOSES AROUND IT: a HAND-SHAPED HOLE through the paper, a hand made of LAMP_CORE light, warm, its finger segments closing over his in 6 frames on ONES, the smoothest motion in the film. Its singed CHAR edge is 8px wide, with ember flecks. His card fingers squeeze back. The second heartbeat locks into phase with his. 'Two.' The squeeze releases his letters to full width, and each letter casts two shadows. He lowers the phone: a pull back to a wide. Scott sits alone on the grass. Beside him, NOTHING: no silhouette and no hole in the wide, only his hand extended slightly to the side, closed on empty air. At the stage lip: TWO RODS, amber and bare, standing together. Cut back to the hands: the light-hand holds. The fire dims, the strobes fade and the lamp goes out, but the hand-shaped light STAYS LIT for 48 frames after everything else is black. It is light with no lamp. Then it goes too. The final chapter card: the TWO OF HEARTS, both pips present, no hole. Then 'THE END' in IM Fell English SC.

sound_design.cue: The lamp hum and room tone (the bed under every interior)
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Two OscillatorNodes: a 50 Hz sine at gain 0.012 and a 100 Hz sine at gain 0.006, with their gain modulated by a 0.7 Hz LFO at depth 0.002, plus brown noise (a 2s AudioBuffer generated with leaky integration from a seeded PRNG) through a BiquadFilter lowpass at 300 Hz, Q 0.5, gain 0.02. Flicker events add a 4ms filament tick: a noise burst through a bandpass at 3 kHz with Q 4. The lamp-off moment is a hard gain cut to 0 in 10ms, preceded by a relay click (a 2ms square pulse through a highpass at 1.5 kHz).

White noise through a bandpass at 2.2 kHz (Q 0.4, gain 0.08), opened as the door plane opens. Droplets: seeded Poisson events at 22 per second, each a sine from 2,800 to 5,200 Hz with an exponential pitch drop of 30% over 25ms and gain 0.04 decaying in 30ms, panned randomly from -0.6 to 0.6 with a StereoPannerNode.

Doorbell: two triangle oscillators, E5 (659.25 Hz) then C5 (523.25 Hz) 0.45s apart, each with a 2x-frequency sine partial at 0.3 gain and an exponential decay over 1.2s, through a lowpass at 4 kHz. Knock: a 60ms sine burst at 140 Hz with a pitch drop to 90 Hz, plus a 15ms noise burst through a bandpass at 900 Hz; the impatient knocking is 5 of these, 0.18s apart, with gain jitter of ±15%.

sound_design.cue: The latch CLICK and the second CLICK
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Click: a 3ms noise burst through a highpass at 2 kHz, plus a bandpass at 1.2 kHz with Q 12 ringing for 40ms. The second click is identical but pitched one semitone down (bandpass at 1.13 kHz), at -6 dB, and hard-panned to the opposite channel, a click from the wrong side. The same two-click asymmetry returns for the bathroom door.

On every 12 fps pose change of a visible joint: a noise burst of 50 to 90ms through a bandpass at 3 to 4.5 kHz (Q 0.7) with gain 0.015 and a fast attack and decay, and the brass pin creak: an FM pair with a carrier at 1,100 Hz and a modulator at 37 Hz, index 120, over 70ms, at gain 0.006. Rods dropping through the lip: a 120ms wooden knock, a sine at 220 Hz decaying in 80ms, plus noise through a bandpass at 700 Hz.

sound_design.cue: Card deal, rod-tick count, and the detuned card
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Card: a 14ms noise burst through a bandpass at 2.5 kHz (Q 1.2), plus a 20ms 120 Hz sine thump. Count tick (on every count cut): a woodblock made of two sines at 1,200 and 1,840 Hz, a 1ms attack and a 60ms exponential decay, gain 0.12. Any count past the true number (the 7th pile, the 5th card, the 5th name) is set to detune -100 cents and run through a ConvolverNode with only the wet signal. It is subtle but wrong.

sound_design.cue: Character type voices (no voice acting: each line's arrival makes a sound)
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: A soft tone per line entry, mixed at -28 dB under the paper sound. Scott: a triangle at A3 (220 Hz) with a 90ms pluck envelope, nervous: a second, quieter retrigger 60ms later. Deena: a square at D4 through a lowpass at 900 Hz, 50ms, a slap. Angelo: a card-snap noise plus a sine at G3 196 Hz, 120ms. Kay: a glass harmonic, a sine at 1,760 Hz with 5 Hz vibrato at ±6 cents, a 300ms attack and a 900ms release. Christof: a 3-note rising triangle arpeggio (C4, E4, G4, 40ms each). Marina: a single pure sine at 880 Hz, exact, 200ms, no vibrato. Dispatcher: a 1ms tick per typed character, noise through a highpass at 5 kHz at gain 0.02.

It uses the tone of the character whose type it borrows (Angelo's G3 for 'Scott.', Deena's square for 'Angelo.'), but REVERSED: the envelope swells from 0 to peak over 400ms and then cuts to 0 in 5ms. It is sent ONLY to a ConvolverNode (dry gain 0) whose impulse response is 2.8s of seeded noise multiplied by an exp(-t*2.2) decay with the left and right channels decorrelated, so it has a room but no position. A StereoPannerNode drifts from -0.8 to +0.8 over the line. At the same moment the room tone ducks by 6 dB for 1s.

sound_design.cue: Heartbeat bed (from the seven hands to the end), and the second heartbeat
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Each beat is two thumps 0.28s apart (lub-dub): a sine at 55 Hz with exponential pitch drop to 38 Hz over 120ms, gain 0.25 then 0.18, through a lowpass at 150 Hz. BPM = 58 + 54*D, scheduled from t. At -30 dB, rising to -14 dB in the kitchen. In the ENDING, a second heartbeat at 63 BPM, panned +0.3, starts out of phase, and its period interpolates to match Scott's over 12 seconds until the thumps coincide exactly on 'Two.'

Gasp: noise through two parallel bandpasses at 700 Hz and 1,200 Hz (Q 6), gain envelope rising over 180ms then cut in 20ms, with a pitch-rising sine at 300 to 420 Hz underneath at -20 dB. Crash: 6 inharmonic sines at 220 Hz times 1, 2.76, 5.40, 8.93, 13.34 and 19.0, with random phases, gain 0.1 each, decays of 0.4 to 1.8s (higher partials decaying faster), plus a 300ms noise burst through a highpass at 1 kHz. A 0.6s silence (master duck to the lamp hum only) is scheduled immediately before.

A sawtooth at 60 Hz through a lowpass at 220 Hz (Q 2), plus a 120 Hz sine at half gain, with a compressor (threshold -30, ratio 4). It sits at -36 dB all night and rises to -12 dB over 2 seconds after the second VOICE line ('The ordinary hum of the refrigerator suddenly feels loud').

sound_design.cue: Gas hiss and the Shepard rise (from the hallway to the explosion)
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Hiss: white noise through a highpass at 4 kHz plus a peaking filter at 7 kHz (+6 dB), gain ramping from 0.01 to 0.12 across the kitchen. Shepard-Risset glissando: 8 sine oscillators an octave apart (base 55 Hz); each frequency is f0 * 2^((k + t/40) mod 8), and each gain is a Gaussian over log-frequency centred on 440 Hz with a sigma of 1.5 octaves, so the pitch rises one octave every 40s endlessly. It sits at -26 dB, rising to -16 dB during the standoff.

sound_design.cue: Oven door, Deena's wound, and the wet flutter
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Oven: a low metal creak, FM with a carrier at 90 Hz, a modulator at 3 Hz and an index of 40 wobbling, over 600ms, then a clunk (a 150 Hz sine decaying in 200ms, plus noise through a lowpass at 400 Hz). Wound: 0.4s of TOTAL silence (master gain 0, even the lamp hum), then a PAPER RIP: noise through a bandpass sweeping from 800 to 4,000 Hz over 180ms (Q 3), with crackle from 1ms clicks at 120 per second. Wet flutter: noise through a lowpass at 600 Hz, amplitude-modulated by a square LFO whose rate slows from 9 Hz to 2 Hz over 3s, then stops.

Flint scrape: noise through a bandpass at 3.5 kHz (Q 2) for 110ms, with a granular crackle of 1ms impulses at random 2 to 8ms intervals, plus a tiny metallic ping (a 6.2 kHz sine decaying in 40ms). The failed strike also has a spark: 3 clicks with no flame. The final strike is the scrape alone, dry, close, panned centre, with all other sound removed 0.5s before it.

Sub: a sine from 60 Hz down to 24 Hz over 1.6s, gain 0.9. Body: brown noise through a lowpass sweeping from 8 kHz to 180 Hz over 3s, into a WaveShaperNode (curve: tanh(3x)) and a compressor (threshold -18, ratio 12). Debris: 40 seeded short crackles. Then tinnitus: a sine at 4,200 Hz at gain 0.05, which sustains while the master runs through a lowpass ducked to 700 Hz and recovers over 6s. This is the 'ear that won't stop ringing' and connects the film's end back to its first frame (the cold open opens on the same tinnitus). The second explosion is the same recipe at -8 dB, with the debris pitched up 20%.

sound_design.cue: Fire, sirens and the final chord
sound_design.web_audio_recipe: Fire: brown noise through a lowpass at 900 Hz with gain modulated by a random 0.3 to 3 Hz walk, plus crackle impulses at 6 to 30 per second (each a 2ms noise burst through a bandpass at 1 to 5 kHz). Distant siren: a sine gliding between 700 and 950 Hz with a 1.2s period, through a lowpass at 1,200 Hz at -30 dB, synced to the strobe. Final: on the hand-close, a warm pad of 4 detuned sawtooths (A2, E3, A3, C#4, each with ±7 cents of detune) through a lowpass at 600 Hz with a 2s attack at -22 dB: 'relief, so sudden it hurts.' On 'Two.' a fifth voice joins at A4 an octave up, and both heartbeats land together. At the fade, everything drops out except the pad, which decays over 4s as the light-hand fades.

feasibility_and_risks:
This style suits code very well. Silhouettes avoid the hardest problem in procedural character work, which is faces: heads are profile-only, so there are no frontal faces to go uncanny. Expression comes from cut-out eye apertures, brow slivers and jaw hinges, which read as deliberate craft rather than a limitation. A single persistent rig per character, the same Path2D parts and pins, keeps the cast consistent across 40+ shots by construction.

REAL RISKS AND HOW TO HANDLE THEM:
(1) SILHOUETTE APPEAL. Hand-writing bezier path data for six appealing, distinct profiles is the single biggest creative risk. Plan: a parametric profile-head generator (a 12-control-point spline with named parameters: brow height, nose length and tilt, lip and chin projection, hair-piece type), iterated on a 'turnaround' test page showing all six heads side by side at three sizes before any shot is built. Read silhouettes as a test sheet: every character must be identifiable in pure black at 120px tall by their outline alone (Deena's bun and zigzag, Angelo's curls and cigarette, Kay's long translucent hair, Christof's biscuit and wide arms, Marina's sleek bob and rings, Scott's height and stoop).
(2) FLAT VECTORS LOOKING CHEAP. This is solved by layering lighting rather than adding detail: paper-fibre multiply, rim light, contact shadows between planes, tissue-gel glow, thin-paper translucency, dust in the beam, gate weave, grain, and the 12 fps puppet stepping. Never ship a plane without its rim light and contact shadow. Flat colour with no texture is the cheap look.
(3) PERFORMANCE. ctx.filter blur and per-frame shadows are expensive. Cache every static plane (with its shadow) to an OffscreenCanvas per shot, and only re-render the moving puppets. Export runs offline at 1080p and does not need real time; the scrubbing preview runs at 960x540.
(4) THE BURN-THROUGH (explosion, curtain). This is a per-pixel noise threshold. Compute it at 480x270 into an ImageData mask, upscale with smoothing, and composite. Noise is precomputed once, so it stays deterministic and is fast enough.
(5) CHRISTOF'S CRUMPLED HEAD. Fake crumples by drawing 9 crease polylines, each with a light-to-dark linear gradient across it, clipped to the head silhouette. This is a 10-minute effect, and in a 0.75s held shot it reads as convincingly damaged paper.
(6) HAND INSERTS (cards, linked hands, lighter, the final hand). These need dedicated 3x-scale hand rigs with 14 finger segments, which take the most rigging time. Build one master hand rig and reskin it per character (rings for Marina, a lattice cuff for Angelo).
(7) DIALOGUE VOLUME. The script is dialogue-heavy, so the type system must be data-driven: a dialogue JSON of {speaker, text (verbatim), startT, emphasis, tearAt} rendered by a per-character style module. Line timing comes from reading speed, not invented pacing.
(8) AUDIO DETERMINISM. Render the whole score with an OfflineAudioContext from seeded buffers to a single WAV and mux it with the video. Do not rely on live AudioContext timing.
(9) READABILITY. The film relies on counting rods and holes, so contrast must be high. The bare rod must be distinct from the coloured rods even in small wides. Test at phone size.
(10) RUNTIME. About 12 minutes at 24 fps is 17,280 frames. At about 150ms per frame offline, that is about 45 minutes of export.

The extra effort is concentrated in a small number of places: the silhouettes, the hand rig, the burn shader and the type system. Everything else is reuse of the same layers and lighting passes.
